rationale: Sector/industry-led hypothesis: use HDFCLIFE as the closest read-through because it is the only same-industry peer and also the strongest graph/correlation neighbor. Add BAJAJFINSV as a diversified financial-services proxy that shares insurance/wealth sensitivity and is also a graph neighbor. Add SBIN to capture broader financial-sector and SBI-group sentiment transmission, especially relevant when headlines are mixed but slightly positive and policy pressure may affect distribution/financial demand across the ecosystem. This set tests whether SBILIFE is primarily driven by life-insurance peer moves plus large-financial sector tone.

Correlation/regime hypothesis: use HDFCLIFE for persistent industry linkage, GRASIM for the strongest recent rolling correlation signal, and TMPV for another high recent correlation and shared sideways regime behavior. This basket is less about business similarity and more about market co-movement structure in a low-volatility, sideways tape. With neutral-to-slightly-positive mood and weak 60d momentum, this set tests whether SBILIFE is currently being driven more by factor/regime flows than by pure sector fundamentals.

Cross-sector defensive/large-cap mood hypothesis: use HDFCLIFE as anchor, WIPRO as a graph neighbor and large-cap low-beta defensive sentiment proxy, and NESTLEIND as another low-volatility defensive consumption bellwether from the same market-cap bucket. Since SBILIFE has low beta, low realized volatility, and mixed headlines with only modest positive mood, its near-term behavior may align with broader defensive large-cap risk appetite rather than only financials. This set tests whether defensive rotation and market mood explain SBILIFE better than direct sector linkages.

Sector-leader and correlation cluster hypothesis: use the closest auto/2W peers and strongest graph-linked names to capture industry demand, pricing, rural recovery, and EV-transition spillovers. HEROMOTOCO has bullish-but-mixed news flow, positive relative strength, and a sideways regime, so the most informative neighbors are the core auto manufacturers with both structural similarity and high observed linkage. M&M has the strongest rolling correlation, BAJAJ-AUTO is a direct 2W competitor, and MARUTI is both a top graph neighbor and a broad passenger-vehicle demand readthrough for discretionary auto sentiment.

Graph-plus-regime hypothesis: combine the highest-conviction graph neighbor with same-industry and same-trend-regime names to model short-horizon co-movement while preserving diversity across vehicle categories. TMPV is the top graph neighbor and shares market-cap/volatility characteristics, EICHERMOT has very high rolling correlation and captures premium motorcycle demand, and TMCV adds commercial-vehicle cycle information that can help identify broader auto demand and macro-sensitive risk-on moves. This set is useful when HEROMOTOCO trades more on market mood and auto-complex flows than on pure 2W fundamentals.

Cross-sector consumption and financing hypothesis: HEROMOTOCO sits in consumer cyclical with bullish sentiment, improving demand narrative, and moderate beta, so adjacent consumer and financing signals may forecast marginal demand better than only auto peers in a sideways tape. TITAN acts as a premium discretionary consumption proxy, INDUSINDBK reflects retail credit/auto financing conditions, and BPCL captures fuel-price sensitivity that influences two-wheeler usage economics and consumer affordability. This diversified set tests whether macro-consumption, financing, and input/fuel context explain HEROMOTOCO better than sector-only neighbors under mixed-to-bullish headlines.

Experiment 1 — Auto peer leadership. BAJAJ-AUTO is in a bullish trend regime with strong 20d/60d momentum and high relative strength vs Nifty, so the most direct forecasting hypothesis is that near-term moves are best explained by industry peers with the strongest and most recent co-movement. M&M, MARUTI, and HEROMOTOCO are the strongest rolling-correlation names over 60d/120d, and HEROMOTOCO/MARUTI/M&M also appear as graph neighbors, reinforcing structural linkage. With news sentiment unavailable, I would treat market mood as neutral and rely more on price-network information; this makes peer confirmation especially important. This set tests whether BAJAJ-AUTO is being driven by shared auto demand, pricing, exports, and premium 2W/PV sector rotation.

Experiment 2 — Two-wheeler/commercial vehicle value-chain read-through. This hypothesis focuses on closer industry transmission rather than broad auto beta. HEROMOTOCO and EICHERMOT are highly relevant same-industry/two-wheeler comparables, while TMCV adds commercial vehicle and broader mobility-cycle information that can capture demand, financing, and rural/urban transport trends. HEROMOTOCO is also a graph neighbor and top correlated name, giving one strong anchor, while EICHERMOT and TMCV add differentiated subsegment signals. With no explicit sentiment data, this basket is useful for inferring implicit market mood from autos themselves: if all three confirm strength/weakness, BAJAJ-AUTO likely follows with higher confidence.

Experiment 3 — Cross-sector risk-on and domestic demand regime. BAJAJ-AUTO sits in a bullish, low-volatility regime and is a mega-cap consumer cyclical name, so it may also respond to broader domestic risk appetite rather than only auto-specific signals. TITAN and TRENT are consumer-facing discretionary proxies for urban consumption strength, while BEL is a graph neighbor and low-volatility mega-cap peer that may proxy for institutional flows into quality large-caps in India. Since sentiment is null, this set assumes mood must be extracted from cross-sector leaders: if discretionary consumption and large-cap momentum leaders remain firm, BAJAJ-AUTO may continue outperforming even without fresh stock-specific news. BEL’s graph linkage also helps retain a network-based anchor despite sector diversification.

Sector-leader banking cluster: use SBIN, HDFCBANK, and AXISBANK because they are the strongest graph neighbors and also the most relevant same-industry / high-correlation names. This set is suited to forecasting ICICIBANK through peer bank co-movement, credit-cycle expectations, and sector rotation effects. It fits the current setup well: ICICIBANK is in a bearish trend regime but has positive 20d momentum and strong relative strength vs Nifty, so tightly linked banking peers can help distinguish stock-specific noise from broad private/public bank moves. Neutral-to-mixed sentiment also argues for leaning on hard peer signals rather than headline direction alone.

Financials risk-appetite transmission set: use BAJAJFINSV, HDFCBANK, and SBILIFE to capture broader financial-services mood beyond pure regional banks. BAJAJFINSV has the highest 60d rolling correlation, HDFCBANK is both a graph and industry anchor, and SBILIFE is a graph neighbor that can proxy institutional flows into defensives within financials. This is a different hypothesis: ICICIBANK may trade not just with bank fundamentals, but with the broader financial complex’s appetite for credit, insurance, and retail-finance exposure. Given mixed headlines with slight positive bias and low beta/low volatility, this set tests whether cross-financial sentiment is more predictive than pure bank peer comparison.

Diverse cross-signal set: use AXISBANK, BAJFINANCE, and TCS. AXISBANK keeps a direct banking read-through, BAJFINANCE adds consumer-credit and retail leverage sensitivity, and TCS contributes large-cap, low-volatility, same-bucket/same-regime market signal to separate broad index-quality flows from bank-specific effects. This is useful because ICICIBANK sits in UltraMega and Low volatility buckets with mixed sentiment and a bearish regime; if headlines are balanced, market participants may price it partly as a stable large-cap rather than only as a bank. This set tests whether combining one close bank peer, one credit-demand proxy, and one broad large-cap risk proxy improves forecast robustness.

Sector-materials hypothesis: use heavy graph/sector neighbors to capture input-cost, commodity-cycle, and building-material demand signals for ASIANPAINT. Neutral/mixed sentiment suggests stock-specific news may not dominate, so upstream/downstream sector read-throughs can be useful. GRASIM and HINDALCO are graph neighbors and same sector; ULTRACEMCO adds construction/housing demand linkage and has strong rolling correlation, making this set a cyclical materials-demand basket.

Correlation-regime hypothesis: emphasize recent co-movement and shared market structure over pure sector match. INDIGO and BAJAJFINSV show very high rolling 60d correlation, while ULTRACEMCO also has strong recent correlation and some end-demand linkage. In a sideways trend regime with balanced sentiment, recent flow-based co-movers may forecast better than fundamental peers.

Consumption/defensive proxy hypothesis: ASIANPAINT often trades with premium consumer names when sentiment is mixed and investors focus on quality, brand strength, and urban demand resilience. HINDUNILVR and NESTLEIND are top correlated consumer defensives, while TRENT adds discretionary retail demand/urban consumption signal. This set tests whether near-term forecasting is better explained by consumption mood than by raw materials peers.

Sector-correlation hypothesis: use TATASTEEL, JSWSTEEL, and GRASIM as the core forecasting neighbors. TATASTEEL and JSWSTEEL are the strongest metal-linked correlations and also the top graph neighbors, making them the cleanest read-through for aluminum and broader ferrous/non-ferrous commodity risk appetite. GRASIM adds a large-cap basic-materials input with strong graph proximity and sector adjacency, helping capture cyclical materials demand beyond pure steel beta. This set fits the current bullish setup: HINDALCO has strong 20d momentum, bullish trend regime, high relative strength vs Nifty, and positive news sentiment, so pro-cyclical materials peers are likely to transmit continuation signals well.

Commodity-macro regime hypothesis: use TATASTEEL, ONGC, and COALINDIA. TATASTEEL remains the anchor because it is the most persistent high-correlation and highest-weight graph neighbor. ONGC and COALINDIA introduce energy and fuel-cost / commodity-cycle information relevant for metals pricing, margin expectations, and macro resource sentiment. This is useful because HINDALCO sits in Basic Materials where earnings often co-move with broader commodity complex behavior, not just same-industry peers. With market mood at 0.74 and headlines skewed bullish, this basket tests whether positive sentiment is being confirmed by a wider commodity upcycle rather than isolated stock-specific optimism.

Risk-regime and cross-sector confirmation hypothesis: use TATASTEEL, SBILIFE, and WIPRO. TATASTEEL is retained as the dominant industrial/commodity transmission node. SBILIFE and WIPRO are direct graph neighbors despite low business overlap, suggesting they may share latent market structure effects such as large-cap flow, institutional rotation, or low-volatility bullish-regime behavior. Since HINDALCO is a large-cap, low-volatility stock in a bullish regime, this set tests whether forecast accuracy improves when combining one strong sector proxy with cross-sector large-cap risk-on indicators. This is especially relevant when sentiment is positive but not unanimous, because cross-sector confirmation can help distinguish broad market accumulation from narrow commodity noise.

Sector-correlation hypothesis: DRREDDY, DIVISLAB, and SUNPHARMA are the cleanest specialty/generic pharma peers for forecasting CIPLA. DRREDDY and DIVISLAB are both strong graph neighbors and also lead the 60d/120d rolling correlations, while SUNPHARMA adds same-industry breadth. With news sentiment neutral and market mood balanced (0.52), idiosyncratic headline spillover is limited, so peer-price discovery and sector rotation should dominate. This set tests whether CIPLA mainly trades as part of the large-cap Indian pharma basket.

Healthcare ecosystem hypothesis: APOLLOHOSP, MAXHEALTH, and DRREDDY capture a broader healthcare demand-and-sentiment channel rather than only pure pharma manufacturing. APOLLOHOSP and MAXHEALTH are top graph neighbors, and APOLLOHOSP also shows strong rolling correlation. In a neutral headline environment, hospital operators can proxy patient flow, treatment intensity, and domestic healthcare spend, while DRREDDY anchors the pharma manufacturing side. This set tests whether CIPLA responds more to healthcare ecosystem strength than to narrow generic-drug peer moves alone.

Defensive low-volatility regime hypothesis: BRITANNIA, TATACONSUM, and DIVISLAB combine one strong graph/industry anchor (DIVISLAB) with two stable consumer-defensive names from the same market-cap/low-volatility neighborhood. CIPLA has very low beta, very low 30d volatility, and a sideways trend regime, so cross-sector defensive flows may matter as much as sector peers when sentiment is neutral. This set tests whether CIPLA behaves like a defensive allocation vehicle, tracking capital rotation across low-volatility staples/healthcare names rather than purely pharma-specific signals.

Sector/correlation hypothesis: Use the closest FMCG and consumption peers because HINDUNILVR is in a low-volatility, sideways regime with mixed but balanced sentiment. NESTLEIND is the strongest graph and correlation neighbor, while BRITANNIA and TATACONSUM reinforce category-level demand and defensive consumption trends. This set tests whether modestly positive fundamentals dominate short-term price pressure through peer confirmation.

Defensive cross-sector risk-on/risk-off hypothesis: Combine the strongest graph neighbor NESTLEIND with SUNPHARMA and ICICIBANK from graph links to capture broader market leadership and rotation effects. Given neutral market mood, low beta, and recent short-term strength but sideways regime, HINDUNILVR may trade as a defensive quality proxy influenced by healthcare defensives and financial market breadth rather than only FMCG peers.

Macro/liquidity and consumer wallet hypothesis: Pair TATACONSUM and ITC as adjacent consumption/defensive signals with RELIANCE as a broad market and household-spend/liquidity proxy. This tests whether HINDUNILVR’s mixed news flow and share-price weakness are being driven less by pure peer moves and more by wider consumer demand, index-level flows, and sentiment spillovers from large-cap leadership. RELIANCE is also a graph neighbor, adding network support.

Hypothesis 1 — Healthcare/industry leadership signal set. Use the closest structural and graph-linked healthcare names to forecast MAXHEALTH. APOLLOHOSP is the strongest choice because it is the only same-industry peer, has the highest graph weight, and shows the strongest rolling correlation to MAXHEALTH over both 60d and 120d windows. CIPLA and DIVISLAB add sector-level defensive healthcare information while also appearing as graph neighbors / same-volatility peers. This set is best if bullish news sentiment for hospitals and healthcare quality names transmits through sector leadership, especially with MAXHEALTH entering Nifty 50 and benefiting from institutional flows. Since MAXHEALTH itself is still in a bearish trend regime despite positive sentiment, these neighbors help test whether sector confirmation is strong enough to overpower the weak price regime.

Hypothesis 2 — Correlation plus regime confirmation set. This set emphasizes realized co-movement and trend/regime matching rather than pure sector similarity. APOLLOHOSP remains the anchor due to very high rolling correlation. TMPV is included because it is one of the top contemporaneous correlated names and sits in the same market-cap bucket. BRITANNIA adds very-low-volatility and bearish-regime similarity, making it useful as a defensive-market proxy for MAXHEALTH’s low-beta, low-volatility behavior. This basket tests whether MAXHEALTH trades more like a defensive quality stock under current market conditions: positive sentiment and mood are supportive, but with the stock still in drawdown, low-volatility regime peers may provide better forecasting power than healthcare names alone.

Hypothesis 3 — Cross-sector defensive/consumption proxy set. This is a broader macro-style neighbor basket designed to capture risk-on defensive demand rather than direct business similarity. TATACONSUM and BRITANNIA represent stable consumption/defensive appetite, while HDFCLIFE adds another low-beta, relatively defensive institutional-quality name from the same market-cap bucket. MAXHEALTH has very low beta, low 30d volatility, positive medium-term momentum, and strong relative strength vs Nifty despite a bearish trend regime, so it may respond to portfolio rotation into steady compounders rather than only healthcare-specific moves. Given the bullish sentiment backdrop and index-inclusion-related support, this set tests whether broader defensive accumulation signals forecast MAXHEALTH better than sector peers alone.

Hypothesis 1 — graph-led mixed signal set. TRENT is in a sideways regime but with strong 20d momentum, high 30d volatility, and deep current drawdown, so I would anchor on the strongest graph neighbors and recent co-movers rather than pure industry peers. TMCV and ETERNAL are both high-weight graph neighbors and also share regime or volatility characteristics, which can help capture broad risk-on/risk-off and discretionary spending appetite. INDIGO has the strongest 60d and 120d rolling correlation to TRENT, making it useful as a non-obvious cross-sector market signal for recent flow alignment. News sentiment is null, so the set leans more on market structure and graph connectivity than narrative.

Hypothesis 2 — consumer discretionary / premium consumption proxy set. TRENT is an apparel retail name in Consumer Cyclical, so a demand-proxy basket may forecast it through discretionary spending strength. TITAN is one of the top static correlations and is a strong premium consumption read-through. M&M and EICHERMOT add auto discretionary demand sensitivity; EICHERMOT is also a graph neighbor and both appear in TRENT’s top correlated names. This set tests whether TRENT trades with premium consumer demand rather than with broad market beta. With no sentiment input, this is a clean fundamental-style consumption hypothesis.

Hypothesis 3 — regime and market-cap similarity set. TRENT has low beta but high realized volatility, large-cap status, and a sideways trend regime after a large drawdown. This basket emphasizes names sharing regime/size/volatility context rather than direct business overlap. JIOFIN is a graph neighbor and shares the high-volatility bucket; GRASIM appears in the same trend regime and has strong 60d rolling correlation; SHRIRAMFIN shares both volatility bucket and large-cap cohort. This set tests whether TRENT is currently being driven more by factor rotation, liquidity, and regime behavior than by consumer-specific information. Null sentiment again argues for emphasizing observable cross-sectional market mood through these regime peers.

Defensive consumer peer set. ITC sits in Consumer Defensive/Tobacco, with very low volatility and a sideways regime. Given bearish news sentiment, the most informative neighbors may be close staples peers that absorb similar institutional flows and defensiveness rotations. BRITANNIA and TATACONSUM are the strongest graph neighbors, while HINDUNILVR is both a top correlated name and in the same sector/trend regime. This set tests whether ITC trades as a staples basket despite stock-specific negative headlines.

Correlation and regime-transmission set. KOTAKBANK is a strong graph neighbor and the highest rolling 60d/120d correlation, suggesting recent macro/liquidity linkage. POWERGRID shares the very-low-volatility bucket and often reflects defensive capital allocation. BHARTIARTL, while not in candidate neighbors, shows strong rolling 60d correlation and similar low-volatility/sideways characteristics; if restricted strictly to candidates, substitute AXISBANK. This hypothesis tests whether ITC is being driven more by market-style factors, defensive flows, and cross-sector risk sentiment than by sector fundamentals alone, especially under bearish mood.

Cross-sector macro and yield proxy set. ONGC and POWERGRID are graph-linked and share low-volatility/mega-cap characteristics; both can capture defensive, dividend, and policy-sensitive market rotation. RELIANCE adds broad market and consumption-energy macro signal, and is also among ITC's top correlated names and same trend regime. With negative sentiment around taxes/excise and weak performance, this set tests whether ITC responds more like a policy-sensitive mega-cap value/defensive trade than a pure staples stock.

Hypothesis 1 — sector and industry transmission. RELIANCE sits in Energy / refining-marketing, with mixed but slightly positive sentiment tied to Jio IPO restructuring and capital activity, while the stock itself remains in a sideways regime with low volatility. A sector-led neighbor set should capture crude/refining beta and domestic energy-policy spillovers. BPCL is the closest same-industry peer, ONGC adds upstream energy sensitivity, and COALINDIA contributes broad energy demand and commodity-linked domestic cyclicality. COALINDIA is also a graph neighbor, which strengthens its inclusion.

Hypothesis 2 — market-structure and correlation signals. Since RELIANCE has low beta, low realized volatility, and a sideways trend, broad market leadership and rolling co-movement may be more informative than pure sector peers. ADANIPORTS has the strongest recent rolling correlation and captures trade/logistics pulse, SBIN appears among top correlated names and reflects domestic credit/risk appetite, and LT is in the same mega-cap cohort while representing capex/infrastructure demand. This set tests whether RELIANCE is being driven more by India macro breadth than by oil-specific factors.

Hypothesis 3 — conglomerate/consumer-tech capital-market narrative. News flow is mixed with a slight positive tilt around Jio IPO progress and restructuring, suggesting that telecom, financialization, and consumer-facing optionality may matter alongside refining. JIOFIN is the most natural adjacent signal given group-level capital-market linkage and is also one of the top correlated names. HINDUNILVR, a graph neighbor, serves as a defensive consumption proxy in a low-volatility sideways tape, while ICICIBANK, also a graph neighbor, captures liquidity and funding conditions relevant to large-cap rerating and capital raising. This set tests whether sentiment transmission from consumer/financial franchises explains RELIANCE better than energy factors.

Sector-correlation hypothesis: use large private banks with the strongest industry linkage to KOTAKBANK. HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, and AXISBANK are same-industry peers, and HDFCBANK/AXISBANK also appear in the correlation structure and graph context. This set is suited to a neutral-to-mixed sentiment tape where stock-specific news is balanced, so relative banking moves, deposit/loan growth expectations, and sector repricing should dominate. Given KOTAKBANK is in a bearish trend regime despite positive 20d momentum, these peers can help distinguish short-term mean reversion from broader private-bank weakness.

Factor-regime hypothesis: combine high rolling-correlation and financial-factor spillover names. BAJAJFINSV has the strongest 60d rolling correlation, HDFCBANK is again highly linked, and M&M adds an external cyclical/credit-demand signal that may capture macro risk appetite and retail/commercial financing conditions. This is useful because news sentiment is mixed rather than decisively bullish, so KOTAKBANK may trade more on style/factor rotation than pure bank fundamentals. The very low beta and low volatility profile also suggest broader factor leaders may offer cleaner signal than only direct peers.

Cross-sector defensive-mood hypothesis: use graph neighbors that reflect index-level and defensive capital rotation. ONGC, ITC, and POWERGRID are all graph-linked to KOTAKBANK and sit in relatively defensive/cash-flow-heavy segments. With market mood only mildly positive (0.54), fair-valuation concerns, and a bearish medium-term regime, KOTAKBANK may co-move with large-cap allocation shifts between defensives and financials. This set tests whether forecast power comes from broad institutional flow and risk-on/risk-off behavior rather than direct banking comparables.

Sector-correlation hypothesis: BAJAJFINSV is in a bearish trend with negative news flow and weak market mood, so the most informative neighbors are highly correlated financials and the strongest graph link. BAJFINANCE is the closest business/market read-through and top correlation; HDFCBANK adds large private-bank credit cycle and risk-appetite signal with very high rolling correlation; HDFCLIFE is also a graph neighbor and captures insurance/financial-holding sentiment spillover relevant to BAJAJFINSV’s conglomerate structure.

Broader financial stress and sector-rotation hypothesis: use a diversified financial basket to capture whether the bearish sentiment is company-specific or part of a wider financial-services repricing. BAJFINANCE remains essential as the strongest related signal; KOTAKBANK contributes defensive large-financial tone and appears in 120d rolling correlation peers; SBIN adds public-sector banking/credit-demand and market-wide financial beta, helping detect if weakness is spreading across banking cohorts rather than only Bajaj-linked names.

Cross-sector macro and market-regime hypothesis: combine graph structure with non-identical but informative cyclical proxies. TMCV is a strong graph/top-correlated neighbor and may reflect domestic growth and financing-sensitive demand. GRASIM adds large-cap cyclical/industrial breadth from the same market-cap bucket, useful for reading macro risk sentiment. HDFCBANK anchors the set with a stable financial benchmark. This trio tests whether BAJAJFINSV is being driven more by broad risk-off growth concerns than by pure sector factors amid bearish headlines and subdued mood.

Sector-leadership hypothesis: use the strongest pharma/healthcare neighbors because DIVISLAB is a low-beta, very-low-volatility large-cap in Healthcare, and news/mood is bullish for the sector. CIPLA is the highest-confidence graph neighbor and also shows strong 60d/120d rolling correlation; SUNPHARMA and DRREDDY are same-industry peers with stable correlation links. This set tests whether positive sector sentiment and analyst optimism propagate through large-cap pharma leaders into DIVISLAB.

Healthcare breadth and defensive-risk-on hypothesis: combine graph neighbors across pharma and hospitals to capture whether DIVISLAB responds more to broader healthcare leadership than to pure generic-drug peer moves. MAXHEALTH and APOLLOHOSP are both strong graph/rolling-correlation healthcare links, while CIPLA anchors same-industry behavior. Given bullish market mood and DIVISLAB's sideways regime with positive 20d/60d momentum, this set tests whether sector breadth confirms upside continuation.

Cross-sector regime hypothesis: mix one core healthcare anchor with non-sector but high rolling-correlation/risk-regime peers to detect style flows into low-volatility large caps. CIPLA provides direct sector information, while TMCV is in the same market-cap bucket and among top correlated names, and GRASIM shares the same sideways trend regime and large-cap profile. This set tests whether DIVISLAB is being driven less by stock-specific pharma factors and more by broad institutional allocation into stable large caps under a bullish sentiment backdrop.

Sector-leader banking set focused on the strongest direct read-throughs for AXISBANK. HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, and SBIN are all same-industry peers, appear in the target's top-correlated/graph-neighbor lists, and capture private-bank plus PSU-bank spillovers. This is the highest-confidence baseline because AXISBANK sentiment is mixed/slightly negative on margin pressure and weak price reaction, so the most useful forecast anchors are other large banks reacting to the same credit, deposit-cost, NIM, and earnings-cycle factors. Including both HDFCBANK and ICICIBANK emphasizes private-bank operating similarity, while SBIN adds broader banking-system tone and state-linked loan/deposit trend information.

Market-regime and financial-beta set aimed at capturing style and risk-on/risk-off transmission rather than only same-industry linkage. BAJAJFINSV and SHRIRAMFIN have very high rolling correlations with AXISBANK over 60d, suggesting shared financial-sector beta under the current sideways regime. HDFCBANK is added as the stabilizing bank anchor and graph neighbor. This set is useful because current news sentiment is not outright bearish but mildly pressured; in such mixed conditions, diversified financial names can capture shifts in lending demand, retail credit appetite, and valuation compression across the broader financial complex better than pure bank peers alone.

Cross-sector macro signal set designed for a sideways, mixed-mood tape. TMPV is a strong graph/top-correlation neighbor and may reflect domestic cyclical demand sensitivity. MARUTI shares the same market-cap bucket/volatility profile and is also a graph neighbor, offering consumer/auto-financing demand clues that often feed bank loan growth expectations. ULTRACEMCO appears in the 120d rolling-correlation list and adds infrastructure/construction cycle information tied to corporate credit and capex sentiment. This diversified basket tests whether AXISBANK is being driven less by bank-specific news and more by broad domestic growth expectations amid neutral market mood.

Sector-correlation hypothesis: TCS is in a bearish trend regime with weak market mood (0.32), and news flow suggests IT-wide pressure rather than a purely idiosyncratic move. The strongest graph and rolling-correlation links are concentrated in large-cap IT peers, so using INFY, HCLTECH, and TECHM should capture common sector de-rating, discretionary tech-spend concerns, and relative rotation inside IT services. This set is best suited for forecasting near-term direction when sector sentiment dominates company-specific developments.

Graph breadth plus defensive market-regime hypothesis: retain the two strongest graph neighbors, INFY and WIPRO, to anchor sector transmission, then add HDFCBANK as a broad-market risk and domestic liquidity barometer. Since TCS has low beta and low volatility but is undergoing a deep drawdown, this combination tests whether its price is being driven by both IT weakness and wider index-level institutional flows. Bearish sentiment in headlines suggests de-risking behavior, so a financial heavyweight can help distinguish sector selloff from general market pressure.

Cross-sector macro-demand hypothesis: pair INFY and LT with SUNPHARMA. INFY captures the strongest peer information from graph/correlation structure; LT can proxy enterprise capex and project spending trends that often co-move with corporate technology budgets; SUNPHARMA, also a graph neighbor, provides a defensive large-cap contrast and can help identify rotation away from growth/IT into defensives under bearish mood. This set is deliberately more diverse and is useful if TCS movement is being shaped by sector weakness plus broader allocation shifts rather than only pure IT peer action.

Sector-plus-correlation hypothesis: use close financial peers with strong recent co-movement to capture lending/credit cycle transmission. AXISBANK is a top 60d rolling correlation name, SBIN is both a same-sector bank and a listed top correlated stock, and BAJAJFINSV has very strong rolling correlation plus financial-services exposure. This set fits the bullish sentiment backdrop for financials and can test whether SHRIRAMFIN follows broad lending-risk-on moves despite its current sideways regime.

Graph-anchored credit ecosystem hypothesis: prioritize names already connected in the graph and industry adjacency. BAJFINANCE is the closest same-industry analogue, JIOFIN is a strong graph neighbor that may reflect market appetite for retail-finance platforms, and TMCV is the strongest graph/correlation neighbor, likely capturing broader cyclical financing demand. With news mood strongly bullish, this basket tests whether SHRIRAMFIN responds more to graph-linked finance/credit sentiment than to pure bank beta.

Diversified cross-signal hypothesis: combine one financial peer, one market-linked cyclicality proxy, and one defensive large-cap signal. HDFCBANK provides sector balance and large-cap financial tone, LT adds capex/investment-cycle sensitivity that can spill into commercial vehicle and wholesale credit demand, and ASIANPAINT offers a lower-beta consumer proxy for broad domestic demand conditions. This set is useful because SHRIRAMFIN has bullish news sentiment but a sideways trend and mixed 20d/60d momentum, so cross-sector leaders may help identify whether the next move is driven by macro demand rather than only finance-specific factors.

Sector-pressure hypothesis: BPCL is in a bearish trend with negative news flow driven by crude-price pressure, result delays, and target cuts. Use closest energy/commodity-linked names to capture refining-marketing and upstream spillovers plus sector mood transmission. RELIANCE is the most direct same-industry anchor, ONGC captures crude-linked upstream sensitivity, and COALINDIA adds a domestic energy complex signal that can reflect broad fuel/commodity sentiment in India. This set leans into bearish sector contagion.

Market-structure and correlation hypothesis: BPCL has meaningful correlation links with SBIN and NTPC, while LT appears in longer-horizon rolling correlations. This trio is a cross-sector macro basket capturing financing/credit conditions, regulated power/energy demand, and capex/infrastructure activity. In a weak sentiment regime, BPCL may trade with broader cyclical and state-linked market factors rather than only pure sector peers. This is a diversified non-industry signal set.

Graph-and-regime hypothesis: incorporate the supplied graph neighbors and similar regime behavior. INDUSINDBK and ADANIENT are strongest graph neighbors, suggesting latent co-movement in the market graph. TMCV adds high-volatility-bucket similarity and a strong candidate for regime-sensitive risk-on/risk-off transmission. With market mood at 0.33 and BPCL in a bearish regime despite short-term momentum bounce, this set tests whether BPCL is best forecast by shared risk appetite, graph adjacency, and volatility clustering rather than sector fundamentals.

Correlation-led, risk-on financials + benchmark proxy. BHARTIARTL has bullish sentiment, positive 20d momentum, strong relative strength, very low beta/volatility, and a sideways regime. A practical forecasting set is to combine its strongest graph/correlation links: ICICIBANK and RELIANCE are the top graph neighbors and also appear in top-correlated names, while BAJFINANCE adds a higher-beta financial risk-appetite signal. This set tests whether Airtel’s next move is being driven less by telecom-specific news and more by broad large-cap market leadership and liquidity-sensitive risk sentiment. The positive market mood supports using pro-cyclical financials as leading indicators, while RELIANCE captures India mega-cap benchmark behavior and digital/consumer exposure that can co-move with telecom demand expectations.

Low-volatility defensive leadership hypothesis. Given SBIN’s sideways regime, low beta, and current drawdown, this set tests whether cross-subsector financial conditions explain returns better than pure bank peers.

Cross-sector macro and market-mood proxy set: use ADANIPORTS as a top-correlated cyclical and explicit candidate neighbor, RELIANCE as an ultra-mega-cap market barometer from the same cap/low-volatility ecosystem, and SUNPHARMA as a defensive low-volatility counterbalance and graph neighbor. With news sentiment clearly bearish and market mood weak, this hypothesis tests whether SBIN is being driven less by bank-specific peer repricing and more by broader risk-on/risk-off flows, economic growth expectations, and defensive rotation. This is intentionally diverse versus the banking sets and suitable for a sideways regime where macro signals can dominate stock-specific follow-through.

Correlation-led Adani complex plus infrastructure confirmation: ADANIENT is the strongest statistical and graph neighbor and captures group-level flow, promoter/news spillover, and risk-on sentiment transmission into ADANIPORTS. INDIGO has very high 60d/120d rolling correlation and acts as a transport-demand proxy, helping test whether bullish port headlines are being confirmed by broader travel/logistics throughput strength. LT adds same-sector industrial/infrastructure exposure and has strong 120d rolling correlation, tying the thesis to capex execution rather than only Adani-specific momentum. This set is suited to the current bullish mood index (0.74), strong 20d momentum, and near-zero current drawdown, while still diversifying beyond pure group linkage.

Industrial-capex demand basket with graph support: BEL is a graph neighbor and same-sector industrial, useful as a regime-level signal for domestic manufacturing/defense order-book strength. NTPC represents power demand and utility capex, often confirming industrial activity and infrastructure utilization that ultimately supports cargo and port throughput. JSWSTEEL adds construction and bulk commodity demand sensitivity, making this a clean test of whether ADANIPORTS is trading as part of a broader India capex and materials upcycle. Given bullish news flow around cargo volumes and strong results, this basket emphasizes macro demand confirmation rather than only stock-specific sentiment.

Risk-on mega-cap flow and financial/liquidity transmission set: JIOFIN and SBIN capture domestic liquidity, credit appetite, and institutional risk-on behavior that often accompanies sustained momentum in large infrastructure-linked names. ADANIENT is included again because it is both the top absolute/rolling correlation name and the most direct graph-linked read-through for Adani ecosystem sentiment, especially important when headlines are mostly positive but include one cautionary promoter-stake-sale item. This set tests whether ADANIPORTS' bullish trend is being driven less by sector fundamentals alone and more by broad market liquidity, conglomerate beta, and financial conditions. It is intentionally cross-sector and complements the more industrial hypotheses above.

Sector-leader continuation under bearish IT sentiment: INFY is in a bearish trend regime with weak 20d/60d momentum and negative news flow centered on growth concerns and target cuts. Use the strongest sector transmission names and graph links to capture read-through from IT services repricing. TCS and TECHM are the top graph/rolling-correlation anchors, while HCLTECH adds same-industry confirmation and shares the bearish regime. This is the purest hypothesis that INFY will continue to trade as part of an IT basket rather than on idiosyncratic valuation support.

Sector plus domestic macro risk filter: bearish sentiment may reflect not only IT-specific downgrades but also broader large-cap risk appetite. Pair TCS, the strongest graph neighbor and sector bellwether, with HDFCBANK and LT to capture domestic investment-cycle and financial-conditions signals. HDFCBANK is already a graph neighbor and shares the bearish trend regime; LT adds a capex/corporate-demand proxy with moderate correlation. This set tests whether INFY weakness is amplified by broad enterprise-spending caution rather than only sector de-rating.

Balanced downside-vs-rotation hypothesis: if market mood remains cautious (0.37), capital may rotate away from weak-momentum IT into defensives, while lower-tier IT names still transmit sector stress. Combine WIPRO and HCLTECH as same-industry/graph-linked spillover channels with HINDUNILVR as a defensive consumption proxy. If INFY underperforms while defensive staples strengthen, this basket can help separate sector-specific pain from broader risk-off rotation. It is deliberately more cross-sector and less concentrated than the pure IT setup.

Auto-cycle transmission with strongest industry anchors. Use HEROMOTOCO and M&M as high-confidence network/correlation anchors: HEROMOTOCO is both a graph neighbor and a top correlated same-industry peer, while M&M has the highest rolling 60d/120d correlation, capturing current auto-demand and sector beta. Add EICHERMOT to inject premium motorcycle/export-cycle read-through, relevant because BAJAJ-AUTO sentiment is bullish on profit beat, exports, and margins. This set tests whether BAJAJ-AUTO’s current bullish regime and strong relative strength are primarily explained by direct auto-industry momentum rather than broader market rotation.

Two-wheeler plus export/value-chain confirmation. HEROMOTOCO remains the core graph-linked two-wheeler proxy; TMCV adds broader mobility, fleet demand, and financing sensitivity; MARUTI brings large-cap auto risk sentiment and is both a graph neighbor and highly correlated over 60d. Given the 0.74 bullish market mood and positive news flow tempered by some margin/buyback caution, this basket is designed to capture whether BAJAJ-AUTO follows a broad auto-complex rally with mixed subsegment confirmation across 2W, PV, and CV. If all three stay constructive, it would support persistence in BAJAJ-AUTO’s uptrend.

Cross-sector quality/risk-on regime hypothesis. Pair one direct auto anchor, HEROMOTOCO, with BEL and TITAN to test whether BAJAJ-AUTO is being driven not only by auto fundamentals but also by institutional flows into low-volatility, high-quality, bullish-regime leaders and discretionary consumption winners. BEL is a graph neighbor and quality large-cap proxy; TITAN represents domestic consumption/risk appetite. This is useful because sentiment is net bullish but not euphoric: strong earnings and broker support may be amplified if broader quality-growth and consumption leadership remains intact. The set distinguishes stock-specific auto strength from market-wide premiumization/risk-on behavior.

Hypothesis 1 — industrial/capex transmission basket. Use ADANIPORTS, LT, and NTPC. BEL sits in Industrials with a sideways regime, positive 20d momentum, low beta, and mixed news where the offering/dilution overhang may be partly offset by broader capex/infrastructure strength. ADANIPORTS and LT are same-sector names and BEL has meaningful statistical/graph ties to ADANIPORTS, while LT is also among top correlated names. NTPC adds a stable power/infrastructure demand signal that often tracks domestic investment appetite. This set tests whether BEL trades more with India capex and project-execution sentiment than with the company-specific dilution headline. In a neutral-to-mixed market mood (0.48), these neighbors should capture broad institutional rotation into defensives/capex beneficiaries.

Hypothesis 2 — graph/flow-driven low-vol mega-cap basket. Use COALINDIA, BAJAJ-AUTO, and ONGC. COALINDIA is BEL's strongest graph neighbor, while BAJAJ-AUTO and ONGC fit the low-volatility / mega-cap / institutional-flow profile that may matter when BEL itself is low beta and in a sideways regime. With mixed sentiment and a likely dilutive offering as the main stock-specific catalyst, BEL may temporarily trade less on defense fundamentals and more on domestic large-cap risk appetite. COALINDIA and ONGC inject commodity/energy-state-owned flow sensitivity, while BAJAJ-AUTO contributes stable large-cap positioning behavior from the same market-cap/volatility bucket. This is a cross-sector regime basket aimed at capturing passive and macro flow effects.

Hypothesis 3 — correlation plus cyclical production basket. Use SHRIRAMFIN, TITAN, and JSWSTEEL. Although less intuitive fundamentally, these names show the strongest rolling correlation structure with BEL over 60d/120d, especially SHRIRAMFIN and JSWSTEEL, while TITAN also appears in the rolling-correlation set and same mega-cap bucket. JSWSTEEL is additionally a graph neighbor, giving this set both statistical and network support. The idea is that in a neutral mood and sideways trend, BEL may respond to latent market factors such as credit conditions, discretionary demand, and industrial production rather than pure aerospace-defense news. This basket is intentionally diverse and tests whether short-horizon forecasting improves by following empirical co-movement instead of sector labels, especially when the news backdrop is mixed and company-specific dilution muddies direction.

Pharma-peer plus emergent healthcare-flow basket. Use CIPLA and DRREDDY as the two closest same-industry transmission names because they are SUNPHARMA’s strongest long-run pharma correlations and should react similarly to positive acquisition-led rerating, margin expectations, and specialty/generics sentiment. Add MAXHEALTH instead of a third pharma name to capture the strongest recent 60-day co-movement and test whether bullish news flow (market mood 0.82) is pulling capital across the broader healthcare complex rather than only within drug manufacturers. This is a high-conviction sector/rolling-correlation hypothesis and is close to prior successful healthcare-oriented setups.

Graph-anchor macro quality basket. Use TCS, ICICIBANK, and RELIANCE because all are graph neighbors with equal weight, ultra-mega-cap liquid leaders, and useful proxies for institutional risk appetite, funding conditions, and broad quality rotation. SUNPHARMA has low beta and low 30-day volatility, so pairing it with other stable large-cap leadership names can help model whether the current bullish move is part of a wider defensive-growth/quality bid rather than purely stock-specific M&A enthusiasm. Positive sentiment around the Organon deal may be amplified if market participants are simultaneously favoring large, cash-generative index heavyweights.

Defensive healthcare-consumption crossover basket. Use APOLLOHOSP, HINDUNILVR, and SBIN to test a different hypothesis: SUNPHARMA’s reaction may reflect a mix of healthcare defensiveness, consumer-staples-style resilience, and domestic liquidity confidence. APOLLOHOSP adds same-sector but different-industry exposure, capturing healthcare demand breadth beyond pharma. HINDUNILVR is a graph neighbor and low-volatility defensive quality name, useful for measuring whether the market is rewarding safety and earnings visibility. SBIN, also a graph neighbor, introduces a domestic risk-on/liquidity gauge; if bullish sentiment is broadening after the acquisition announcement, bank leadership can help explain continuation versus a short-lived pharma-only spike.

Peer-contagion / governance-isolation hypothesis: use ICICIBANK and AXISBANK as the two strongest graph neighbors to capture same-industry banking spillover, then add KOTAKBANK because it is both same-industry and a strong 60d/120d rolling correlation name. With HDFCBANK in a bearish trend regime, deep drawdown, and negative governance-heavy news flow, this trio tests whether weakness is idiosyncratic to HDFCBANK leadership uncertainty or a broader private-bank rerating. If all three banks move in sync, sector contagion is dominant; if HDFCBANK diverges, the news overhang is likely stock-specific.

Financial-regime / sentiment transmission hypothesis: combine BAJAJFINSV and BAJFINANCE to capture broader financial-services risk appetite, then add ICICIBANK as the clean banking anchor. BAJFINANCE and BAJAJFINSV are graph-linked to HDFCBANK, while BAJAJFINSV also appears in strong rolling-correlation history. In a bearish mood environment with put-heavy positioning and governance concerns, this basket checks whether HDFCBANK is reacting as part of a wider financials de-risking move rather than purely bank-specific stress. It should be useful because these names share sector exposure but represent different subsegments of financials.

Cross-sector macro filter hypothesis: keep AXISBANK as the direct banking comparator, then add INFY and LT as ultra-large-cap macro/cycle proxies from the same market-cap ecosystem. AXISBANK preserves industry signal, INFY offers a lower-beta risk-appetite/defensive growth read and is also a graph neighbor, while LT adds domestic capex and broad cyclical demand sensitivity. Given bearish sentiment but still positive 20d momentum versus weak 60d momentum, this trio helps detect whether HDFCBANK's short-term moves are driven by local governance headlines or by broader shifts in institutional positioning across Indian large caps.

Auto-cluster confirmation with controlled concentration. Use TMCV, MARUTI, and M&M because they are the strongest graph/rolling-correlation neighbors and sit in the same industry, making this the purest sector-similarity test. This set is well aligned with the current bullish sentiment and strong market mood: if analyst upgrades and top-gainer behavior in EICHERMOT reflect a broad auto upcycle rather than idiosyncratic news, these three should transmit the signal best. It also directly tests whether the recent positive 20d momentum and high relative strength vs Nifty are being reinforced by the wider OEM basket despite the stock being in a sideways regime overall.

Premium discretionary spillover with one industry anchor. Use HEROMOTOCO, TITAN, and TRENT to capture consumer demand breadth rather than only auto-beta. HEROMOTOCO keeps a same-industry two-wheeler anchor and is also a prior successful neighbor, while TITAN and TRENT represent premium consumption and discretionary spending strength. This hypothesis fits the bullish news tone: raised targets and constructive outlook for EICHERMOT may be partly driven by improving affluent-consumer demand, not just vehicle-cycle signals. It also reduces overreliance on highly correlated auto names and is suitable because EICHERMOT has low beta and a sideways trend regime, where broader consumption proxies can add signal diversity.

Regime-matched cross-sector quality basket. Use BAJAJFINSV, ASIANPAINT, and MARUTI to combine one strong auto read-through with two large-cap quality proxies from similar regime buckets. MARUTI is the sector/correlation anchor and a major graph neighbor; BAJAJFINSV adds financial-risk appetite and large-cap quality sentiment; ASIANPAINT adds a durable-demand and economic-confidence proxy, and it was part of the best past experiment for EICHERMOT. This set tests whether the stock’s bullish sentiment and favorable mood index are being supported by a broader large-cap risk-on environment rather than a narrow industry move. It is a diversified hypothesis for a sideways-trend, medium-volatility stock where cross-sector confirmation may outperform pure peer clustering.

Insurance-led transmission hypothesis. Use SBILIFE as the primary peer because it is the only same-industry name and has the strongest stable correlation signal with HDFCLIFE (about 0.59 long-term, 0.66 over 60d, 0.62 over 120d). Add BAJAJFINSV because it is the highest-weight graph neighbor and a same-sector diversified financial proxy, useful for capturing broad financial-services risk appetite. Add HDFCBANK to reflect ecosystem linkage and the supportive headline flow tied to HDFC Bank investment, while also representing the bearish financial trend regime. With sentiment neutral-to-mixed, this set tests whether HDFCLIFE will follow sector/parent financial stabilization more than standalone revenue-miss pressure.

Bearish-regime factor and correlation spillover hypothesis. Use SBILIFE again for direct insurance signal, but pair it with TECHM and BRITANNIA to capture cross-sector defensive factor rotation during a bearish regime. TECHM is a graph neighbor and shares the same bearish trend regime and medium volatility profile, while BRITANNIA is a same-market-cap bearish-regime defensive consumption proxy. Since news flow is mixed rather than decisively negative, this basket tests whether HDFCLIFE price action is being driven less by insurance fundamentals and more by broad quality/defensive de-rating and macro style rotation.

Financial stress vs. mean-reversion hypothesis. Use INDUSINDBK and KOTAKBANK as large financial-sector comparables in the same bearish regime to capture banking-system sentiment transmission, and combine them with BAJAJFINSV as the strongest graph-linked diversified financial. This set intentionally excludes the direct insurance peer to test whether HDFCLIFE's weak 60d momentum and deep drawdown are mainly functions of broader financials repricing rather than life-insurance-specific fundamentals. Given the market mood index of 0.52 and mixed headlines, this trio is suited for detecting whether neutral sentiment leads to recovery alongside financials or whether sector-wide weakness continues to dominate.

Hypothesis 1 — premium discretionary demand with graph confirmation. TRENT sits in Consumer Cyclical/Apparel Retail with mixed but still supportive corporate-action news flow: dividend, bonus shares, AGM-related interest, and brokerage attention offset by EPS miss and recent volatility. With market mood mildly constructive at 0.56 and TRENT showing strong 20d momentum but a sideways broader regime after a deep drawdown, a premium-consumption basket can test whether the stock responds more to demand proxies than to its own noisy news tape. TITAN is a strong premium consumption read-through and was part of a prior relatively successful TRENT setup; M&M adds broader discretionary spending and consumer confidence sensitivity and also worked in past experiments; EICHERMOT is both a top correlated name and a graph neighbor, giving the basket a network anchor. This set emphasizes consumer wallet strength and resilient discretionary demand while still respecting graph structure.

Hypothesis 2 — rolling-correlation and regime transmission. TRENT’s static beta is low, but realized volatility is high and recent relative strength versus Nifty is very strong, suggesting idiosyncratic leadership embedded inside a sideways regime. Mixed sentiment argues for using market-structure companions rather than only sector peers. INDIGO has the strongest 60d and 120d rolling correlation, GRASIM also ranks at the top of recent rolling correlation and shares the same trend regime, and JIOFIN is a graph neighbor that also shares the high-volatility cohort. Together, these three test whether TRENT is currently trading as part of a broader liquidity/rotation cluster rather than purely as an apparel retail story. Mildly positive market mood supports this cross-sector co-movement hypothesis, especially after TRENT’s large drawdown and rebound behavior.

Hypothesis 3 — graph-led large-cap high-volatility basket. TRENT has high 30d volatility, a sizable current drawdown, and a sideways regime, while headlines are mixed rather than cleanly bullish. In such conditions, graph neighbors and regime peers may carry more predictive information than fundamental similarity alone. TMCV is the strongest graph neighbor and also among top static correlations; ETERNAL is another highest-weight graph connection and shares regime/volatility characteristics; SHRIRAMFIN contributes a same large-cap bucket and same high-volatility-bucket signal, helping capture broader risk appetite and flow-driven behavior. This set is intentionally less consumer-specific and instead tests whether TRENT’s next move is governed by network connectivity, risk-on/risk-off mood, and large-cap volatility clustering under a neutral-to-slightly-positive sentiment backdrop.

Sector-plus-correlation hypothesis: use GRASIM, TMPV, and JSWSTEEL. GRASIM is the strongest same-industry anchor and has the highest rolling correlation with ULTRACEMCO, making it the cleanest peer transmission channel for earnings-led bullish sentiment. TMPV is the top raw correlation name and a strong graph neighbor, so it should capture shared cement/building-material demand. JSWSTEEL adds a high-weight graph connection and broader construction-material cycle exposure, testing whether positive news in ULTRACEMCO is really part of a wider infrastructure/materials bid. This set leans into the bullish news flow and 0.73 market mood, while respecting the still-bearish trend regime by focusing on names most likely to co-move if sentiment follow-through persists.

Macro-capex confirmation hypothesis: use LT, ADANIPORTS, and M&M. A prior successful run already showed LT and M&M can help beat baseline, so this variant keeps that cross-sector macro structure and adds ADANIPORTS as an industrial throughput/logistics proxy. LT is especially compelling given very high recent rolling correlation and its role as a construction execution signal; ADANIPORTS captures trade and freight intensity that often confirms industrial demand; M&M adds domestic cyclical demand and rural/investment sentiment. This basket tests whether ULTRACEMCO’s bullish earnings reaction is being validated by a broader capex and domestic demand cycle rather than by cement peers alone. It is intentionally diversified across sectors to reduce pure peer redundancy while still aligning with positive market mood.

Regime-balanced mega-cap hypothesis: use MARUTI, KOTAKBANK, and GRASIM. ULTRACEMCO sits in a bearish trend regime but has positive 20-day momentum, strong relative strength vs Nifty, and supportive news sentiment. This set is designed to capture that tension. GRASIM remains the industry anchor for direct cement linkage. MARUTI contributes same-regime and cyclical consumption sensitivity, helping test whether the recent bounce is part of a wider domestic recovery trade. KOTAKBANK adds credit and financing-cycle information from the mega-cap universe, useful because cement demand often follows project financing and economic confidence. This is a more defensive cross-factor basket than a pure materials set, built for a mega-cap, medium-volatility stock where sentiment is bullish but the broader technical regime is not fully repaired yet.

Healthcare-core with strongest recent co-movement: CIPLA, MAXHEALTH, and SUNPHARMA combine the highest-confidence graph/correlation signals around DIVISLAB under a bullish sentiment backdrop (market mood 0.79). CIPLA is the clearest anchor with the highest graph weight (0.527) plus strong 60d rolling correlation, making it the best direct peer for specialty/generic pharma behavior. MAXHEALTH adds the strongest 60d rolling correlation overall and shares the very-low-volatility profile, useful because DIVISLAB is in a sideways but positively trending low-vol regime where defensive healthcare flows may matter. SUNPHARMA adds same-industry breadth and graph support, capturing whether bullish broker upgrades for Divi’s are part of a broader pharma rerating rather than a stock-specific move.

Industry-plus-macro rotation basket: CIPLA, DRREDDY, and TMCV test whether DIVISLAB’s upside is driven by pure pharma confirmation plus broader large-cap risk-on allocation. CIPLA and DRREDDY are both same-industry peers and graph neighbors, giving a strong pharmaceutical manufacturing signal. TMCV is not a healthcare peer but sits in the same market-cap bucket and same sideways trend regime, which helps capture cross-sector institutional rotation into large caps during a bullish tape. This is especially relevant because DIVISLAB has positive 20d/60d momentum, low beta, and very low volatility; if sentiment remains strong, it may move with both pharma leaders and broad quality-large-cap flow.

Healthcare ecosystem with defensive low-vol confirmation: APOLLOHOSP, MAXHEALTH, and CIPLA express a broader healthcare-chain hypothesis rather than only API/generics peer matching. APOLLOHOSP and MAXHEALTH both show strong rolling correlation links to DIVISLAB and represent healthcare demand/defensive allocation proxies, while CIPLA remains the graph-weighted pharma anchor. This set is suited to the current setup where DIVISLAB is still in a sideways regime and only modestly below prior highs; bullish news sentiment may not immediately produce an isolated breakout, but could instead appear first as synchronized strength across low-vol healthcare names. The basket therefore tests whether Divi’s responds more to healthcare ecosystem momentum and defensive institutional positioning than to narrow same-industry moves alone.

Auto-core continuation hypothesis: MARUTI has bullish news flow and strong 20d momentum, while sector mood is constructive despite the broader bearish trend regime. This set leuses the strongest industry/graph relationships to test whether positive earnings reaction and auto-strength continue through the most synchronized peers. M&M is the highest-weight graph neighbor and a top 60d/120d correlation name; EICHERMOT has the strongest rolling correlation profile; HEROMOTOCO adds same-industry breadth with medium-volatility alignment and meaningful graph proximity. Relative to prior successful sets, this rotates HEROMOTOCO in for TMPV/TMCV to test whether listed 2W/auto discretionary demand confirms MARUTI’s move better than commercial/passenger peer alternatives.

Auto plus supply-chain breadth hypothesis: News sentiment is bullish, but there are mentions of resistance and mixed broker notes, so a slightly broader auto basket may capture whether MARUTI’s move is sector-wide or narrowing. M&M and EICHERMOT remain anchor names due to graph weight and rolling correlations. TMCV is added as a same-industry candidate from a previously effective setup, offering exposure to broader vehicle-cycle and operating-demand signals. This set tests whether MARUTI’s path is best explained by synchronized auto ecosystem strength rather than only direct passenger-car peers.

Consumer discretionary cross-signal hypothesis: MARUTI’s sentiment is bullish, but the stock still sits in a bearish long-term regime with a sizable current drawdown, so confirmation from adjacent consumption and financing proxies may matter. TITAN is a graph neighbor and same-sector discretionary large-cap, useful as a demand-confidence readthrough. KOTAKBANK captures vehicle financing, household liquidity, and retail credit conditions that can lead auto demand. M&M remains the core anchor because it is both the strongest graph neighbor and highly correlated auto peer. This diversified set tests whether MARUTI is responding to a broader consumer spending and credit recovery rather than pure industry co-movement.

Hypothesis 1 - Policy-sensitive PSU energy basket: ONGC has strongly bullish news sentiment from the royalty-rate cut, so the cleanest test is to pair it with names most exposed to government-policy and PSU allocation flows. COALINDIA and NTPC are the two strongest graph neighbors and top historical correlates, while BPCL adds same-sector energy linkage. This set tests whether ONGC's next move is primarily driven by a PSU-energy rerating channel rather than broad market beta. The fit is reinforced by ONGC's low beta, very low volatility, bullish trend regime, and prior success of PSU-oriented baskets in past experiments.

Hypothesis 2 - Low-volatility defensive institutional rotation: ONGC's profile is unusually defensive for an energy stock - mega-cap, very low volatility, low beta, positive 20d/60d momentum, and near highs versus its 1-year range. With market mood strongly risk-positive, institutions may be favoring stable, dividend-like large caps rather than only commodity plays. POWERGRID and ITC match the low-volatility/defensive allocation style, while KOTAKBANK adds a mega-cap quality financial proxy that is also a graph neighbor. This set tests whether ONGC is participating in a broader defensive mega-cap rotation amplified by positive sentiment, not just energy-specific news.

Hypothesis 3 - Cyclical metals and infrastructure transmission: If the bullish ONGC news is being interpreted as part of a wider commodity and industrial upcycle, then cross-sector cyclicals should help explain returns. HINDALCO has the strongest rolling 60d/120d correlation to ONGC, TATASTEEL is also a top correlated cyclical peer, and ADANIPORTS captures trade/logistics and infrastructure demand transmission. This basket is intentionally different from PSU defensives: it tests whether ONGC's upside is less about royalty policy alone and more about broad pro-growth, commodity-linked market mood spilling into energy, metals, and infrastructure names.

Auto-cycle plus financing confirmation hypothesis: use direct industry peers and a key lending proxy to test whether TMCV’s bullish post-demerger rerating is sustained by genuine CV demand recovery rather than listing euphoria. M&M and MARUTI provide same-industry large-cap auto read-throughs with different end-market mixes, while SHRIRAMFIN adds a high-relevance financing signal for commercial vehicle demand and has both strong static correlation (~0.67) and graph support (~0.67 weight). This set is distinct from prior pure auto-peer bundles by replacing EICHERMOT with a credit-sensitive demand channel. With sentiment strongly bullish and market mood at 0.87, the hypothesis is that positive news converts into durable earnings/margin follow-through only if auto peers and vehicle-finance conditions confirm.

Domestic capex and freight activity hypothesis: test whether TMCV is trading as a broader infrastructure-and-mobility beneficiary rather than only as an auto name. ULTRACEMCO has the strongest recent rolling correlation (~0.80), likely reflecting construction/infra demand that drives truck utilization and fleet replacement. INDIGO contributes a graph-linked mobility and economic activity signal (~0.61 graph weight), while EICHERMOT adds a high rolling auto correlation (~0.79) and graph proximity (~0.62). This combination blends graph neighbors and correlation leaders to capture freight, travel, and discretionary transport intensity. In a bullish news regime, if TMCV’s rerating is really macro-demand led, these cyclical activity proxies should improve forecast power.

Risk-on discretionary rerating hypothesis: examine whether TMCV’s relative strength vs Nifty (1.34x) is being driven by broad large-cap cyclical appetite in a sideways market rather than sector-specific fundamentals. TRENT and ETERNAL are graph-supported/high-beta consumer demand proxies, with ETERNAL the strongest graph neighbor (~0.77) and TRENT also directly connected (~0.60). BAJAJFINSV adds financial-conditions and wealth-effect sensitivity with meaningful correlation (~0.62) and similar volatility characteristics. This diversified cross-sector basket intentionally leans into the very bullish market mood and positive headline flow to test whether TMCV is participating in a wider consumption-and-liquidity rerating wave post listing.

Auto-demand plus financing sensitivity hypothesis: use M&M, HEROMOTOCO, and SHRIRAMFIN. M&M and HEROMOTOCO are same-industry names, both aligned with TMPV’s medium-volatility and sideways-regime profile, while M&M is also a top graph neighbor and strong rolling-correlation style peer. SHRIRAMFIN adds a credit/vehicle-financing channel that can matter when headlines are mixed and investor confidence is not fully committed. With sentiment neutral-to-mixed and market mood only modestly positive, this set tests whether TMPV’s next move is driven less by pure stock-specific demerger noise and more by underlying auto demand plus financing conditions.

Consumer-discretionary spillover hypothesis: use INDIGO, TITAN, and MARUTI. INDIGO has very strong recent 60d rolling correlation and serves as a mobility/travel demand proxy; TITAN is a meaningful graph neighbor and captures upper-end discretionary spending tone; MARUTI adds direct passenger-vehicle sector read-through. This is intentionally broader than a pure auto basket, reflecting the mixed headline backdrop: recent bullish impulses from easing geopolitical stress and short-term price spikes, but also profit-taking and weak post-demerger returns. If TMPV is trading as a discretionary-consumption sentiment asset rather than only on fundamentals, this trio should be informative.

Macro-cyclical overlay hypothesis: use LT, ULTRACEMCO, and EICHERMOT. LT and ULTRACEMCO are among the strongest top-correlated names and both appear in graph/peer structures, making them useful proxies for broader domestic investment-cycle and cyclical risk appetite. EICHERMOT keeps an industry anchor inside autos while diversifying away from TMPV’s exact business mix. Given TMPV’s sideways trend regime, medium volatility, strong 20d momentum but weaker 60d momentum, and mixed sentiment, this set tests whether near-term forecasting improves when TMPV is modeled as part of a broader cyclical basket responding to macro relief rather than as a pure passenger-auto story.

Private-bank core with broad financial transmission. Use SBIN, HDFCBANK, and AXISBANK. This is the highest-conviction sector/correlation hypothesis: SBIN and HDFCBANK are the strongest graph neighbors (0.81 and 0.60), while AXISBANK is a proven successful neighbor in past ICICIBANK runs and has very strong 60d/120d correlation. With ICICIBANK in a bearish trend regime but still showing positive 20d momentum and strong relative strength vs Nifty, this set tests whether mixed sentiment is being resolved through banking-system leadership rather than stock-specific headlines. Neutral-to-slightly-positive market mood suggests peer confirmation matters more than macro panic, so the model can learn whether analyst upgrades and hedge-fund interest are echoed across private/public bank leaders.

Idiosyncratic-vs-sector isolation with a defensive control. Use AXISBANK, INDUSINDBK, and SUNPHARMA. This is a diversification hypothesis built around one strong banking anchor plus one alternative private-bank read and one low-vol defensive non-financial. AXISBANK is both highly correlated and previously successful for ICICIBANK; INDUSINDBK gives same-industry exposure without being as collinear as stacking only the largest peers; SUNPHARMA adds an UltraMega, low-volatility defensive benchmark from outside financials. Given mixed headlines for ICICIBANK—upgrades and investor engagement offset by insider selling, bearish technicals, and earnings disappointment—this set helps distinguish whether weakness is bank-specific, private-bank-wide, or simply part of a broader quality/defensive rotation under a neutral market mood.

Cross-financial risk-appetite and quality-rotation signal. Use BAJAJFINSV, SBILIFE, and HDFCBANK. BAJAJFINSV has the strongest rolling 60d correlation among listed peers, SBILIFE is a graph neighbor and captures insurance/savings-flow behavior, and HDFCBANK anchors the private-bank signal. This hypothesis goes beyond pure bank-peer matching and tests whether ICICIBANK is trading as part of the broader financial-services complex rather than only on bank fundamentals. Correlation-regime stability hypothesis: use ULTRACEMCO, INDIGO, and SHRIRAMFIN. Staples core + graph-weighted defensive cluster. Low-volatility quality rotation with healthcare cross-signal. Financial-complex spillover setup. Defensive yield and state-owned flow basket: use POWERGRID, BPCL, and BEL. Low-volatility quality basket hypothesis: ITC and TATACONSUM provide same-sector consumption signals, with TATACONSUM also supported by strong 60d/120d correlation. Graph-led retail-credit continuation. Use TMCV, JIOFIN, and BAJFINANCE. Cross-sector demand and economic-activity breakout basket. Use TMCV, LT, and EICHERMOT. Industry-leader bank basket. Financials-plus-broad risk-factor hybrid. Use HDFCBANK, BAJAJFINSV, and M&M to capture the strongest recent rolling-correlation structure and macro credit-cycle spillovers. Defensive-rotation plus bank anchor. Use AXISBANK, ITC, and POWERGRID to test whether KOTAKBANK is being driven by index-level capital rotation rather than only bank fundamentals. Graph-and-correlation capex confirmation: ADANIPORTS and SBIN are already strong graph neighbors of LT, giving direct network evidence of shared flow and financing dynamics. Sector-activity and transport linkage hypothesis: INDIGO has extremely high recent rolling correlation with LT, BEL is a same-sector industrial peer that can capture domestic capex/defense ordering tone, and TATASTEEL adds metals input-cycle sensitivity for project execution. Graph-core with regime confirmation: use TMCV and TRENT as the two strongest graph neighbors, then add JIOFIN as an additional graph-linked large-cap/high-volatility risk-on proxy. Correlation-plus-consumption hypothesis: combine TMCV with M&M and ASIANPAINT. Consumer discretionary demand chain with graph support: pair TRENT and TITAN as premium/discretionary consumption bellwethers and add EICHERMOT, which is also a graph neighbor and part of the best prior ETERNAL setup. Auto-demand with financing confirmation: M&M and HEROMOTOCO are the cleanest industry/graph anchors for TMPV, matching its auto exposure, medium-volatility profile, and sideways regime. Consumer-discretionary risk-on basket: TITAN is a strong graph neighbor and often captures upper-end discretionary spending tone, while INDIGO has the strongest recent 60d rolling-correlation relationship and can proxy mobility/travel demand sensitivity. Macro-cyclical overlay with industry anchor: LT and ULTRACEMCO are both top static-correlation names and graph-adjacent cyclical indicators, useful if TMPV is trading more as a broad domestic risk-on/capex-sensitive asset than as a pure auto name. Hybrid graph-plus-cross-sector macro basket. Pure private-bank transmission hypothesis. Broader financial-beta and retail credit-cycle hypothesis. BAJAJFINSV and SHRIRAMFIN have extremely strong recent rolling correlations with AXISBANK, indicating shared exposure to retail credit demand, spread compression, and risk appetite within financials. Cross-sector financed-consumption and market-regime hypothesis.
