MARUTI is already a graph neighbor, and TITAN adds a high-quality sentiment-sensitive consumption signal. This set tests whether financed consumption leads repricing in private lenders when pure banking signals are noisy.

Auto-peer + graph-structure hypothesis: use MARUTI, EICHERMOT, and TMPV. This is the most direct structural set because MARUTI is the strongest graph/rolling-correlation anchor for M&M, TMPV has the highest raw correlation and very strong 60d linkage, and EICHERMOT is both a graph neighbor and same-industry proxy. With news sentiment neutral and no M&M-specific catalyst, price discovery is more likely to come from shared auto demand, OEM/supply-chain dynamics, and sector rotation rather than idiosyncratic news. This set tests whether M&M’s bearish regime but positive 20d momentum rebound is best explained by immediate industry peers and graph-linked auto structure.

Consumer-cyclical demand mix hypothesis: use TITAN, HEROMOTOCO, and BAJAJ-AUTO. TITAN is a meaningful graph neighbor despite not being a direct auto manufacturer, which suggests M&M may co-move with broader discretionary consumption and premium spending patterns. HEROMOTOCO and BAJAJ-AUTO add two-wheeler and retail vehicle demand sensitivity from the same sector/industry family. Given neutral headlines and a market mood index of 0.5, this basket assumes M&M trades less on company news and more on household demand resilience, festive/rural consumption tone, and discretionary risk appetite. It is intentionally distinct from a pure correlation basket by blending graph structure with consumption proxies.

Macro transmission hypothesis: use KOTAKBANK, ADANIPORTS, and ULTRACEMCO. M&M has low beta, is in a bearish trend regime, and prior runs showed cross-sector macro sets can outperform, suggesting financing and domestic activity conditions may be more informative than pure sector clustering. KOTAKBANK captures auto-loan and credit-cycle sensitivity, ADANIPORTS proxies logistics/trade/industrial throughput relevant for CV and rural-commercial demand, and ULTRACEMCO reflects domestic capex and construction activity that can spill into tractors and utility vehicle demand. With sentiment neutral and no stock-specific signal, this set tests whether M&M is currently driven by macro breadth rather than auto peers alone.

Sector-plus-energy linkage hypothesis: NTPC, BPCL, and COALINDIA. NTPC is the mandatory anchor because it is POWERGRID’s strongest graph neighbor (0.837), same sector/industry peer, and the top correlation name across static and rolling windows. BPCL and COALINDIA add fuel-chain and energy-cycle confirmation: both are among the top correlated candidates, and COALINDIA is also a graph neighbor. With POWERGRID in a bullish trend regime, strong 20d/60d momentum, very low volatility, and mildly bullish news flow around revenue beat, dividend support, and power-demand optimism, this basket tests whether POWERGRID is currently trading as part of a broader regulated-power and domestic energy complex rather than as a standalone utility defensive. The set should capture sentiment spillover from energy demand, grid utilization, and PSU-style income/defensive flows.

Low-volatility defensive rotation hypothesis: NTPC, ITC, and ONGC. Prior successful runs already suggest NTPC plus defensive/quality large caps can explain part of POWERGRID’s behavior. Here NTPC remains the sector control, while ITC is a graph neighbor and classic low-volatility defensive proxy; ONGC is also a graph neighbor, shares the same volatility bucket and bullish trend regime, and adds commodity-linked cash-flow sensitivity without becoming too cyclical. Given POWERGRID’s low beta (0.24), very low realized volatility, mega-cap status, and mildly bullish market mood (0.63), this set tests whether investors are treating POWERGRID as part of a broader institutional quality-and-yield basket during constructive but selective risk appetite. It is a different angle from pure sector similarity: less about electricity transmission alone, more about defensive leadership and state-linked large-cap rotation.

Infrastructure and capex breadth hypothesis: NTPC, ADANIPORTS, and BEL. NTPC again anchors the utility-specific signal, but ADANIPORTS and BEL broaden the explanatory set toward domestic infrastructure, logistics, and strategic-capex leadership. Both fit POWERGRID’s mega-cap and bullish-trend context; BEL also aligns with low-vol/quality characteristics better than a more volatile infra proxy would. News sentiment is mildly bullish with emphasis on grid expansion, energy/AI power demand, and favorable positioning, so this basket tests whether POWERGRID’s strength is being driven by a wider India capex and state-linked infrastructure narrative rather than only regulated utility fundamentals. The inclusion of a strong graph anchor plus two cross-sector capex proxies creates a more diversified hypothesis than the defensive or energy-complex sets.

Utility-energy core continuation hypothesis: NTPC has bullish sentiment, strong market mood (0.72), a bullish trend regime, positive 20d/60d momentum, and very low volatility, so the cleanest setup is to anchor on its strongest structural and graph-linked energy peers. POWERGRID is the highest-confidence neighbor because it is the only same-industry/same-sector peer and the strongest graph neighbor (0.837), likely capturing regulated utility flow and PSU defensiveness. ONGC adds broad energy complex sensitivity and has the second-highest graph weight (0.592), while COALINDIA contributes fuel-chain/input-cost and PSU-energy sentiment transmission with both high static correlation and graph support (0.413). This is also validated by the best prior successful NTPC experiment.

Defensive mega-cap low-volatility rotation hypothesis: NTPC’s news tone suggests investor confidence, analyst/model-portfolio support, and steady corporate signaling, which can attract institutional flows into low-beta, low-volatility mega caps beyond pure utility linkage. POWERGRID remains the anchor because of same-industry relevance and dominant graph weight. KOTAKBANK and ITC are both graph neighbors (0.4 each), large liquid defensive names, and fit the very-low-volatility / quality-allocation regime that may co-move with NTPC when market mood is constructive but investors still prefer stability. This set tests whether NTPC’s move is driven more by defensive allocation behavior than by sector-specific power fundamentals.

Cross-sector cyclical capex spillover hypothesis: Despite being a regulated utility, NTPC shows notable rolling correlation with cyclical industrial names, especially JSWSTEEL, suggesting it may currently be participating in a broader infrastructure/power-buildout trade. With bullish sentiment around strategic project MoUs and supportive market mood, NTPC may be reacting not just as a defensive utility but as a beneficiary of capex optimism. COALINDIA bridges energy demand and fuel supply into the thesis, while ADANIPORTS captures infrastructure/logistics risk-on flows and JSWSTEEL reflects the strong recent rolling-correlation regime. This set is intentionally more macro-cyclical and distinct from the pure utility basket.

Core materials transmission hypothesis: use the strongest structurally linked names where GRASIM should co-move with sector demand and building-materials fundamentals in a low-volatility, sideways regime. ULTRACEMCO is the highest-conviction same-industry anchor and also shows the strongest rolling correlation support. HINDALCO and JSWSTEEL are top graph neighbors and same-sector large caps, capturing broader basic-materials risk appetite and cyclical commodity positioning. This set leans into neutral/mixed sentiment by emphasizing stable fundamental linkages over headline-sensitive cross-sector names; it should work if the Reuters paints-management concern is secondary to broader materials-cycle behavior.

Paints-and-construction spillover hypothesis: mixed headlines specifically mention concern around the paints chief exit and valuation reassessment, so include ASIANPAINT as the most direct sentiment read-through into GRASIM’s paints exposure. Pair it with ULTRACEMCO to capture cement/construction demand and with TATASTEEL as a graph neighbor tied to capex/building-cycle momentum. This basket tests whether GRASIM’s recent 20d rebound but still-flat 60d setup is being driven by ecosystem sentiment across housing, construction inputs, and downstream decorative/building products rather than pure sector beta.

Cross-sector low-beta regime hypothesis: GRASIM has low beta, low 30d volatility, and a sideways trend regime, so its near-term moves may partly reflect broader large-cap allocation and defensive-vs-cyclical rotation rather than only materials signals. SBILIFE and WIPRO match the low-volatility/large-cap/regime profile and can proxy domestic risk appetite plus quality-factor behavior, while ULTRACEMCO keeps one high-signal industry anchor in the basket. This diverse set is suitable if neutral market mood (0.5) and mixed news cause GRASIM to trade more on broad portfolio flows and valuation normalization than on commodity-specific shocks alone.

Hypothesis 1: Use a transport-and-infrastructure stress basket to separate airline-specific weakness from broader mobility demand softness under the current bearish news flow and low market mood (0.28). ADANIPORTS and LT are same-sector Industrials names with strong 120d rolling correlations to INDIGO, and both can proxy logistics throughput and domestic capex/trade resilience. TMCV is the strongest graph neighbor and also a same-market-cap / high-volatility peer proxy for cyclical transport demand. If these three remain relatively stable while INDIGO weakens, the model can infer that recent negative headlines are more about crude, forex, and airline margin pressure; if they weaken together, that supports a broader macro-demand slowdown signal.

Hypothesis 2: Build a financial-conditions and discretionary-demand basket to capture whether bearish sentiment around overseas leisure travel and earnings pressure is spilling into domestic consumption and credit. BAJAJFINSV has the highest 60d rolling correlation and shares the bearish trend regime, making it a strong cross-market risk/liquidity proxy. SHRIRAMFIN adds another credit-sensitive large-cap from the same market-cap universe, while TRENT is a graph neighbor and a clean discretionary consumption barometer. In a weak mood regime, this set tests whether INDIGO is reacting to broad tightening in household demand/financing conditions versus idiosyncratic airline cost shocks.

Hypothesis 3: Use a graph-plus-cross-sector cyclical basket for a more thematic signal blend suited to mixed short-term momentum (positive 20d, negative 60d) within an overall bearish regime. JIOFIN and ETERNAL are graph neighbors, giving direct network proximity to INDIGO's recent behavior, while EICHERMOT adds a mobility/discretionary demand signal from the same large-cap bucket. This trio is designed to detect whether the stock's drawdown is beginning to mean-revert on management/news stabilization, or whether negative sentiment is broadening into consumer mobility and financing-linked risk appetite. The graph anchors help retain local market structure information while EICHERMOT broadens the demand read-through.

Pure FMCG peer-strength hypothesis: use HINDUNILVR, BRITANNIA, and TATACONSUM. NESTLEIND sits in a bullish trend regime with strong 20d/60d momentum, positive relative strength vs Nifty, and strongly bullish news flow around earnings. HINDUNILVR is the highest-conviction anchor because it is the top graph neighbor and also the strongest 60d/120d rolling-correlation name, suggesting persistent co-movement. BRITANNIA and TATACONSUM are same-industry or adjacent packaged-food/staples peers with consistently high historical correlation, making this the cleanest read on whether positive sentiment in staples continues to transmit across the FMCG basket. This is distinct from prior successful sets by emphasizing the two strongest direct food peers together with the graph anchor.

Defensive rotation plus sector breadth hypothesis: use HINDUNILVR, ITC, and ASIANPAINT. With market mood at 0.78 and NESTLEIND being a low-volatility large-cap defensive name near highs, the stock may be benefitting from institutional rotation into quality domestic franchises, not just packaged-food fundamentals. HINDUNILVR again serves as the graph-led anchor. ITC broadens the consumer-defensive sector exposure while still staying close to staples flows. ASIANPAINT adds a cross-industry but consumer-linked, low-volatility large-cap signal that can capture broader domestic demand confidence and quality-compounder buying. This set tests whether NESTLEIND responds to a wider defensive-consumption rerating under bullish sentiment.

Graph/regime transmission hypothesis: use HINDUNILVR, GRASIM, and SBILIFE. This is the most cross-sector set and is designed to test whether NESTLEIND’s move is being driven by market regime and large-cap style factors rather than only sector peers. All three appear as graph neighbors, with HINDUNILVR the strongest by weight and GRASIM/SBILIFE representing large-cap, lower-volatility institutional flow proxies. In a bullish mood backdrop with low realized volatility and strong momentum, NESTLEIND may co-move with other favored quality compounders and defensive leaders across sectors. This basket therefore captures sentiment transmission from staples leadership into broader large-cap defensive/risk-on positioning.

Sector-input-cost and construction-demand basket. ASIANPAINT sits in a mixed-news, neutral-mood setup with recent rebound and pricing support, but demand recovery remains uncertain. This suggests upstream materials and building-cycle names may still carry useful signal. GRASIM and HINDALCO are graph neighbors and same-sector peers, helping capture chemical/feedstock and commodity-cost transmission, while ULTRACEMCO adds housing/construction end-demand linkage and is also a strong recent correlation name. This is a refined version of the best prior materials hypothesis, leaning on graph structure plus cyclical demand read-through.

Recent co-movement and regime-aligned flow basket. With ASIANPAINT in a sideways regime, low beta, moderate 20d momentum, and mixed headlines, short-horizon forecasting may benefit more from market-structure co-movers than pure industry matches. INDIGO and BAJAJFINSV have very high rolling 60d correlation with ASIANPAINT, while EICHERMOT shares volatility bucket and trend-regime similarity and is also a graph neighbor. The idea is that in a neutral market mood, common institutional flow and factor rotation can dominate stock-specific fundamentals.

Defensive-consumption plus materials hedge. Mixed sentiment for ASIANPAINT suggests balancing demand-sensitive and defensive signals. HINDUNILVR is one of the top correlated names and shares the same sideways regime, offering a consumer-staples demand proxy. NESTLEIND adds another large-cap defensive consumption signal with meaningful correlation, while TATASTEEL contributes graph-neighbor and same-sector cyclicality to capture raw-material and industrial-demand pressure. This diversified trio tests whether ASIANPAINT trades more like a resilient consumption franchise or a materials-linked cyclical during the current recovery phase.

Sector-leader contagion under bearish IT sentiment: use INFY, TCS, and TECHM. HCLTECH is in a bearish trend regime with weak 20d/60d momentum, deep current drawdown, and strongly negative news flow focused on guidance cuts and sector-wide IT selling. These three are the most natural transmission channels because they are same-sector/same-industry peers, top graph neighbors, and the strongest rolling-correlation names. INFY and TCS have the highest graph weights and strongest 60d/120d co-movement, while TECHM broadens the enterprise IT-services demand signal. This tests the hypothesis that HCLTECH is mainly being driven by sector de-rating and synchronized earnings-expectation compression rather than idiosyncratic stock-specific noise.

Bearish regime plus macro-risk spillover basket: use INFY, KOTAKBANK, and ONGC. With market mood extremely weak and headlines implying risk-off behavior, HCLTECH may reflect not just IT stress but broader macro deleveraging. INFY preserves the strongest direct sector linkage from the graph network, while KOTAKBANK adds a domestic financial-conditions proxy from the same mega-cap and bearish-regime cohorts, and ONGC adds commodity/macro sensitivity that can capture inflation, energy-price, and cyclical risk appetite shifts. This diversified set tests whether HCLTECH weakness is amplified by cross-asset stress and market-wide sentiment deterioration rather than pure software-services fundamentals.

Cross-cycle demand read with IT plus domestic capex/consumption proxies: use TECHM, LT, and MARUTI. Negative semantic sentiment suggests doubts about recovery, so a useful alternative is to combine one strong graph neighbor from IT (TECHM) with non-IT demand proxies. LT represents enterprise capex and infrastructure spending, which can correlate with broader corporate technology budgets and business confidence, while MARUTI captures domestic discretionary demand and cyclical sentiment. This basket is intentionally more diverse than pure peer sets and tests whether HCLTECH is being priced off a wider slowdown in business investment and demand confidence during a bearish market mood, not only sector-specific earnings pressure.

Hypothesis 1 - Policy-sensitive PSU upstream/utility transmission: Use COALINDIA, NTPC, and BPCL to capture the strongest state-linked and energy-complex read-through into ONGC after the royalty-cut news. Bullish sentiment and very high market mood suggest investors are rewarding government-policy beneficiaries and stable PSU cash-flow names. COALINDIA and NTPC are the two strongest graph/correlation neighbors, while BPCL adds direct oil-chain sector linkage. This set tests whether ONGC’s move is primarily explained by a policy-driven rerating across PSU energy and adjacent regulated cash-flow names.

Hypothesis 2 - Defensive mega-cap institutional rotation: Use POWERGRID, ITC, and KOTAKBANK to model ONGC as a low-beta, very-low-volatility mega-cap benefiting from broad institutional allocation rather than only oil fundamentals. The sentiment backdrop is strongly bullish, and ONGC’s low beta, shallow current drawdown, and bullish trend regime fit a defensive quality rotation framework. KOTAKBANK and ITC are graph neighbors from prior successful setups, while POWERGRID matches the PSU/low-volatility profile. This set tests whether ONGC is trading like a stable yield-plus-quality large cap under risk-positive but selective flows.

Hypothesis 3 - Cyclical commodity/risk-on spillover with trend confirmation: Use HINDALCO, TATASTEEL, and ADANIENT to capture ONGC’s participation in a broader pro-cyclical, bullish macro tape. ONGC has positive 20d/60d momentum and strong relative strength versus Nifty, while rolling correlations point to HINDALCO and TATASTEEL as meaningful non-energy companions. ADANIENT adds a graph-neighbor/risk-on proxy tied to capital-cycle and commodity enthusiasm. This set tests whether ONGC’s upside is being reinforced by wider cyclicals and market mood, not just sector-specific news.

Pharma + healthcare momentum basket focused on short-horizon sentiment transmission from the strongly bullish Organon acquisition news. CIPLA and DIVISLAB are among SUNPHARMA's strongest same-industry/same-sector correlations, while MAXHEALTH has the strongest 60-day rolling correlation, making it useful for capturing recent healthcare risk-on rotation rather than only long-run pharma linkage. With SUNPHARMA already in a bullish trend regime, low volatility, and showing strong relative strength vs NIFTY, this set tests whether positive deal sentiment spills across both drug manufacturers and adjacent healthcare leaders. It also differs from prior peer baskets by replacing DRREDDY with DIVISLAB to emphasize a cleaner mix of structural industry co-movement plus emergent rolling-correlation behavior.

Graph-anchor mega-cap quality basket designed to capture whether SUNPHARMA's move is partly driven by broader institutional allocation into low-volatility ultra-mega names during a bullish market mood (0.84), not just pharma-specific excitement. TCS, ICICIBANK, and RELIANCE are all graph neighbors with equal weight, and each sits in the same market-cap ecosystem that often shares liquidity, benchmark flow, and foreign institutional participation dynamics with SUNPHARMA. This hypothesis is especially relevant because SUNPHARMA has very low beta and low 30-day volatility, so cross-sectional quality/defensive leadership may explain part of its forecast path after the acquisition announcement.

Defensive healthcare-consumption crossover basket that blends sector adjacency with defensive demand proxies. APOLLOHOSP adds same-sector but different-industry healthcare services exposure, HINDUNILVR brings a graph-linked defensive consumption signal, and SBIN contributes another graph neighbor representing domestic liquidity and risk appetite transmission. The idea is to test whether SUNPHARMA's bullish response is reinforced by a broader defensive-quality rotation across healthcare and staples, while banking exposure helps identify whether the market interprets the acquisition as growth-positive and financing-friendly. This set is intentionally more cross-sector than pure-correlation baskets, giving a diversified hypothesis around sentiment persistence and market mood spillover.

Auto-core with strongest co-movement. MARUTI has mixed but still constructive setup: strong 20d momentum, relative strength >1, and positive earnings/sales headlines, but bearish broader trend regime and analyst caution argue for using the most synchronized auto names rather than broad macro proxies. M&M is the highest-weight graph neighbor and strongest structural link; EICHERMOT has the strongest rolling 60d/120d correlation; HEROMOTOCO adds same-industry breadth plus meaningful graph proximity. This tests whether MARUTI’s next move is mainly explained by sector-wide auto demand and discretionary mobility sentiment despite downgrade noise.

Auto basket with passenger/commercial cycle confirmation. News sentiment is neutral-to-mixed, so a useful alternative is to keep the two strongest anchors but replace 2W discretionary exposure with a vehicle-cycle confirmation name. M&M and EICHERMOT remain because of top rolling correlations and graph support. TMCV adds same-industry diversification tied to broader transport and fleet demand, helping test whether MARUTI’s rally is broadening across the auto complex or facing upside hurdles after a sharp rebound. This is a sector-similarity plus correlation-similarity hypothesis with slightly wider cyclical breadth.

Consumer/macro cross-signal set. Because MARUTI is in a bearish trend regime with low beta and mixed headline sentiment, its path may depend less on pure peer sympathy and more on Indian consumption, financing conditions, and premium discretionary demand. TITAN is already a graph neighbor and a strong consumer discretionary read-through; KOTAKBANK captures auto-financing and retail credit conditions; ADANIPORTS serves as a macro activity/logistics proxy. This tests whether MARUTI trades as a broader consumption-and-liquidity story rather than only an auto-sector trade, especially when positive fundamentals are offset by valuation/downgrade concerns.

Financial-core continuation hypothesis: BAJAJFINSV is the mandatory anchor given the highest graph weight and strongest structural/rolling correlation to BAJFINANCE, making it the clearest transmission channel for earnings/dividend-led sentiment. HDFCBANK adds a high-confidence banking proxy with very strong 60d/120d rolling correlation and graph-neighbor status, useful for capturing system credit and liquidity tone. AXISBANK complements with another large private bank showing strong recent rolling correlation and the same sideways-regime backdrop, helping test whether the current bullish news flow and 0.76 market mood can push BAJFINANCE out of consolidation through broad private-financial strength rather than only group-level spillover.

NBFC-plus-cyclical confirmation hypothesis: BAJAJFINSV again serves as the core graph-linked parent/affiliate signal. SHRIRAMFIN is the only same-industry peer, so it provides the cleanest read on retail-credit and NBFC-specific sentiment transmission. TMCV, a top-correlated non-financial name and major graph neighbor, introduces cross-sector cyclical demand confirmation; if BAJFINANCE’s recent strength is part of a broader domestic risk-on move rather than a narrow post-results rally, TMCV should help capture that. This set is intentionally diversified across direct industry, financial complex, and cyclical macro sensitivity under the current bullish sentiment backdrop.

Regime-diversified macro credit hypothesis: HDFCBANK and INDUSINDBK are both graph-connected/same-sector banking signals that can reflect loan growth, deposit conditions, and competitive financial sentiment while BAJFINANCE remains in a sideways trend regime with positive short-term momentum. JIOFIN adds a higher-volatility same-sector fintech/financial-services signal from the same volatility bucket, useful for detecting whether the bullish news tone is spilling into more risk-sensitive financial names. This trio avoids repeating the most obvious group anchor and instead tests whether market mood 0.76 is broadening across the financial ecosystem, especially into banks plus emerging financial platforms.

Sector-plus-correlation hypothesis. MAXHEALTH is the essential same-industry anchor and strongest graph neighbor, giving direct hospital-facility read-through. CIPLA adds a high 60d rolling correlation and same-sector defensive healthcare exposure, while DIVISLAB contributes 120d correlation support plus graph linkage. With APOLLOHOSP in a bullish trend regime, very low beta/volatility, strong relative strength, and positive news flow around profit growth/dividend/corporate catalysts, this trio tests whether the stock is primarily being driven by healthcare sector leadership reinforced by bullish sentiment.

Low-volatility institutional-quality rotation hypothesis. MAXHEALTH keeps the healthcare anchor, but BRITANNIA and TATACONSUM introduce non-healthcare defensive compounders that share the very-low-volatility profile and both appear as graph neighbors. Given the bullish market mood index and APOLLOHOSP's strong momentum with low beta, this set tests whether price discovery is being influenced less by pure sector moves and more by broader fund rotation into stable, high-quality, low-volatility names during risk-on but selective markets.

Cross-sector leadership and capital-flow hypothesis. MAXHEALTH again grounds the model in same-industry fundamentals, while BAJFINANCE and BAJAJFINSV capture premium-growth financial leadership and institutional risk appetite. Both finance names are among the stronger candidate relationships/top correlations, and their inclusion probes whether APOLLOHOSP is trading like a broader market favorite rather than only a hospital operator. This is especially relevant under bullish news sentiment and supportive market mood, where corporate catalysts can amplify flows into quality growth franchises across sectors.

Insurance-plus-distribution hypothesis: HDFCLIFE is the mandatory same-industry anchor and strongest graph neighbor, while ICICIBANK and HDFCBANK capture bancassurance/distribution health, credit demand, and broad financial-system sentiment. With SBILIFE in a sideways, low-volatility regime, 20-day momentum mildly positive but 60-day momentum still negative, and news flow mixed with a slight positive tilt, this set tests whether near-term repricing is driven less by pure insurer fundamentals and more by bank-led distribution flows and financial-sector risk appetite. It also avoids repeating the prior KOTAKBANK variant while keeping the financial transmission channel intact.

Graph-structure and large-cap factor hypothesis: HDFCLIFE remains the industry core signal, while GRASIM brings the strongest 60-day and top 120-day rolling correlation support, and BAJAJFINSV is both a graph neighbor and diversified financial-services proxy. This basket leans into the idea that SBILIFE, as a low-beta large-cap in a sideways regime with moderate relative strength vs Nifty, may be trading as part of a broader large-cap factor cluster rather than solely on insurance news. Mixed sentiment and market mood around 0.55 suggest macro/portfolio rotation effects could dominate stock-specific headlines, making graph and rolling-correlation links particularly useful.

Defensive cross-sector mood hypothesis: HDFCLIFE anchors industry read-through, while WIPRO and NESTLEIND represent low-volatility defensive large-cap behavior and risk-on/risk-off rotation proxies. SBILIFE has low beta, low realized volatility, and a sideways trend; in that context, mixed headlines with only a slight positive tilt may not be enough to generate a clean sector move, so broader defensive-market mood may explain returns better. WIPRO is also a graph neighbor, which gives this otherwise cross-sector set structural support, and NESTLEIND adds a stable consumption defensive signal from the large-cap universe.

Sector-stress continuation hypothesis: use TCS, TECHM, and WIPRO to maximize transmission of IT-services weakness into INFY. This basket leans into the bearish news tone, weak 20d/60d momentum, and the current bearish trend regime. TCS and TECHM are the strongest graph/correlation anchors, with TCS carrying the top graph weight and highest rolling correlation, while WIPRO adds breadth as another same-industry spillover channel. Compared with the prior HCLTECH-TCS-TECHM test, swapping in WIPRO creates a slightly broader sector basket and may better capture diffuse sector de-rating rather than only top-tier peer moves.

Sector-plus-domestic risk appetite hypothesis: use TCS, HDFCBANK, and BHARTIARTL. TCS preserves the strongest sector signal for INFY, while HDFCBANK adds large-cap domestic financial conditions and risk-on/risk-off information; it is also a graph neighbor and shares the bearish trend regime. BHARTIARTL introduces a non-IT but resilient large-cap growth/defensive proxy, helping separate INFY-specific IT weakness from broader institutional rotation. With market mood at 0.32 and headlines skewing bearish, this trio tests whether INFY underperformance is mainly sector contagion or part of a wider large-cap style shift.

Cross-sector defensive-rotation hypothesis: use HCLTECH, HINDUNILVR, and SBIN. HCLTECH provides same-industry confirmation and is a strong graph-linked peer in the same bearish trend regime, while HINDUNILVR captures defensive consumption rotation and SBIN captures cyclical domestic beta/risk appetite from financials. This is intentionally less concentrated in IT, suited to the mixed-but-bearish sentiment backdrop where analyst cuts and new lows may trigger allocation away from export IT into defensives or domestic cyclicals. The basket can help detect whether INFY moves are being driven by sector downgrades versus broader portfolio rebalancing across defensives and financials.

Pure sector-stress hypothesis: use TCS, INFY, and TECHM because they are WIPRO's strongest same-industry and graph-linked peers, with TCS/INFY/TECHM also leading rolling correlation lists. Given bearish news flow, weak guidance, insider-selling pressure, and a low market mood index of 0.28, this set tests whether WIPRO's next move is primarily explained by synchronized IT-services sentiment and sector demand repricing rather than broader macro rotation. It is distinct from prior successful sets by replacing defensive cross-sector names with a third IT peer to maximize industry signal concentration.

Sector-plus-demand-cycle hypothesis: use HCLTECH, INFY, and LT. HCLTECH and INFY are strong graph/same-industry neighbors, while LT adds a cross-sector enterprise transformation and capex proxy. In a bearish setup with sideways trend regime, negative 60d momentum, and current drawdown near -24.5%, this basket tests whether WIPRO weakness is being driven by both peer IT derating and softer corporate spending appetite. It also builds on a previously successful HCLTECH-INFY-LT pattern, but keeps the emphasis on two direct IT read-throughs plus one macro-demand signal.

Risk-off rotation hypothesis: use TCS, SBILIFE, and NESTLEIND. TCS anchors the core IT correlation signal, while SBILIFE and NESTLEIND represent large-cap defensive, lower-volatility risk-off behavior that may matter for a low-beta stock like WIPRO. With sentiment clearly bearish and the stock in a sideways regime after a deep 1y drawdown, this set tests whether WIPRO is trading less like a pure tech beta and more like a defensive large-cap exposed to broad market mood and liquidity preferences. This is intentionally diversified versus the all-IT and capex-sensitive variants.

Pure banking stress-propagation hypothesis: use ICICIBANK, AXISBANK, and HDFCBANK. ICICIBANK and AXISBANK are the two strongest graph neighbors, while HDFCBANK is a same-industry large-cap banking bellwether and has already appeared in the best prior SBIN setup. With news sentiment bearish and market mood weak at 0.28, this trio tests whether SBIN’s recent profit-miss/margin-pressure driven selloff is part of a broader private-bank/public-bank earnings repricing rather than stock-specific noise. In a sideways regime with low volatility, tight peer banks may provide the cleanest signal for 20-day forecast transfer.

Broader financial-services spillover hypothesis: use SBILIFE, BAJFINANCE, and SHRIRAMFIN. SBILIFE and BAJFINANCE are both graph neighbors, and SHRIRAMFIN has the strongest rolling 60d/120d correlation profile to SBIN among provided names. This basket intentionally moves beyond pure banks into insurance and NBFC/financing, testing whether bearish sentiment is being transmitted through overall financial risk appetite, credit-cycle expectations, and valuation compression across financials. Given SBIN’s sideways trend, low beta, and still-positive 20d momentum, this set can reveal whether broader financial-services leadership or weakness explains incremental moves better than direct bank peers alone.

Cross-sector macro regime hypothesis: use ADANIPORTS, RELIANCE, and SUNPHARMA. ADANIPORTS is among the top correlated names, while RELIANCE and SUNPHARMA are ultra-mega/low-volatility peers that can proxy broad market risk appetite and defensive rotation. In a mixed-to-negative sentiment backdrop, this trio tests whether SBIN is being driven less by banking fundamentals and more by macro growth expectations, index-level flows, and defensive-versus-cyclical positioning after the sharp two-session drop. This is a deliberately diversified alternative to sector-only models and can be useful if bank-specific signals are already crowded or if SBIN’s low beta makes broader regime cues more predictive.

Pure sector-contagion hypothesis under bearish IT sentiment: TCS headlines are dominated by 52-week lows, IT weakness, and concern over revenue decline, while the stock remains in a bearish trend regime with weak 60d momentum and deep drawdown. This set uses the strongest and most stable industry transmission channels: INFY, HCLTECH, and WIPRO. INFY is the top graph neighbor and highest rolling correlation name; HCLTECH and WIPRO add same-industry breadth while preserving high network relevance. The idea is that in a low market mood regime, near-term price formation for TCS is most likely explained by synchronous repricing across Tier-1 IT services peers rather than idiosyncratic company news.

IT-plus-macro demand confirmation hypothesis: Keep INFY as the essential sector anchor, but pair it with LT and ICICIBANK to capture broader enterprise spending and domestic business-cycle effects. LT can proxy capex, infrastructure digitization, and large transformation pipelines; ICICIBANK can reflect credit appetite, corporate activity, and risk sentiment. This is useful because TCS has a positive 20d rebound inside a clearly bearish 60d trend, so the question is whether any stabilization is being validated by macro-sensitive leaders or is just sector oversold noise. Bearish sentiment suggests macro confirmation matters more than usual, and INFY preserves the graph-based IT contagion signal.

Defensive rotation and relative-allocation hypothesis: TCS is low beta and low volatility, yet still under heavy bearish sentiment and valuation pressure. This set tests whether TCS is being treated as a failed defensive within mega caps by pairing the core IT read-through from INFY with defensive low-volatility leaders HDFCBANK and SUNPHARMA. Both are relevant from the same market-cap/defensive flow context, while INFY keeps the strongest graph-neighbor sector signal. If TCS tracks INFY more closely, sector stress dominates; if it diverges toward HDFCBANK/SUNPHARMA behavior, allocation rotation and broad risk-off positioning may be the stronger explanatory driver.

Sector-capex hypothesis: use ADANIPORTS, LT, and INDIGO. BEL sits in Industrials/Aerospace & Defense with a sideways regime, positive 20d momentum, and low beta/low volatility. LT and ADANIPORTS are same-sector names that should transmit broad domestic capex, infrastructure execution, and government spending signals relevant for BEL. INDIGO adds a more direct aerospace/aviation demand proxy, offering a cleaner read on air-travel and aerospace sentiment than generic mega-caps. This set is useful when news sentiment is mixed: possible equity-supply overhang/dilution-type pressure argues for including broad sector leaders, while supportive headlines and relative strength suggest BEL may still trade with policy/capex beneficiaries. ADANIPORTS is also a graph neighbor, reinforcing structural linkage.

Graph-flow and regime hypothesis: use COALINDIA, BAJAJ-AUTO, and ONGC. This basket leans into BEL's strongest graph connections and its low-volatility, mega-cap, sideways-regime behavior. COALINDIA is the top graph neighbor, BAJAJ-AUTO is also a graph neighbor and shares the low-volatility/large-cap institutional-flow profile, while ONGC adds energy-price and state-owned risk-appetite transmission. With market mood only mildly positive (0.52) and headlines mixed, BEL may behave less like a pure defense name and more like a low-beta domestic large-cap held in common institutional baskets. This set tests whether forecast power comes from macro flow, commodity sensitivity, and government-linked sentiment rather than direct industry mapping.

Correlation-cross-sector hypothesis: use SHRIRAMFIN, TITAN, and JSWSTEEL. BEL's strongest rolling correlations are with SHRIRAMFIN and TITAN over 60d, and JSWSTEEL is both a strong 60d correlation name and a graph neighbor. This combination intentionally avoids pure sector matching and instead captures current market leadership, credit/risk appetite, discretionary demand tone, and cyclical industrial production. In a mixed-news environment where stock-specific headlines can distort BEL short-term, cross-sector correlated leaders can provide a stronger signal for direction if BEL is trading with broader market rotation. JSWSTEEL also ties back to capex and industrial-cycle sensitivity, helping anchor the set to BEL's underlying macro exposure.

Sector-plus-credit confirmation hypothesis: TMCV’s strongly bullish news flow around the CV demerger/listing may persist only if both auto demand and vehicle financing remain supportive. M&M and EICHERMOT are same-industry peers that capture broader auto-cycle follow-through, while SHRIRAMFIN adds a highly relevant CV financing signal with one of the strongest observed relationships to TMCV (top static correlation ~0.67 and graph weight ~0.67). This set leans into the positive sentiment and 0.87 market mood, but tests whether optimism is backed by fundamental demand/credit transmission rather than just listing-premium enthusiasm.

Graph-led risk-on discretionary basket hypothesis: TMCV may currently be trading as part of a broader large-cap domestic demand and risk-on rerating cluster in a sideways regime. TRENT and INDIGO are direct graph neighbors, useful as high-beta consumption/travel demand proxies, while BAJAJFINSV adds financial-conditions sensitivity and meaningful correlation similarity (~0.62). With sentiment strongly bullish and short-term momentum positive despite weak 60d momentum, this basket tests whether TMCV’s near-term path is better explained by broad cyclical appetite, liquidity, and consumer confidence than by pure auto-peer co-movement.

Core auto peer convergence hypothesis: Use direct industry comparables to test whether TMCV’s post-demerger rerating normalizes into sector-led price discovery. MARUTI and BAJAJ-AUTO provide large-cap same-industry read-throughs from different vehicle mix exposures, while EICHERMOT contributes both same-industry relevance and strong recent rolling correlation support (~0.79 over 60d) plus graph linkage (~0.62). In the context of bullish news and expected CV margin expansion, this set isolates whether TMCV’s forecast is best driven by auto-sector operating momentum and peer valuation convergence rather than cross-sector risk sentiment.

Sector-plus-correlation hypothesis: use GRASIM, JSWSTEEL, and TMPV. Bullish sentiment and a strong market mood index of 0.74 suggest ULTRACEMCO may respond best to a materials-chain basket that captures both direct peer sympathy and construction-cycle beta. GRASIM is the strongest same-industry anchor and has the highest rolling 60d correlation, making it the clearest read-through for cement pricing and demand. JSWSTEEL is the strongest graph neighbor by weight and adds broader construction/materials-cycle information. TMPV is the top raw correlation name and also a graph neighbor, reinforcing the signal. This set tests whether the recent positive earnings and broker-driven tone is being transmitted primarily through the building-materials and industrial commodity complex.

Cross-sector capex-demand hypothesis: use LT, ADANIPORTS, and M&M. ULTRACEMCO has bullish news flow but remains in a bearish trend regime, so a pure peer basket may miss macro confirmation. LT contributes infrastructure execution and project pipeline exposure, with very high rolling correlation to ULTRACEMCO. ADANIPORTS captures freight, logistics, and industrial throughput that often lead cement dispatch strength. M&M is a graph neighbor and adds domestic cyclical demand, rural confidence, and capex sensitivity from a different sector. This basket is designed to detect whether the bullish narrative is really a broader India investment-cycle and demand-recovery signal rather than just sector momentum.

Regime-balanced mega-cap hypothesis: use MARUTI, KOTAKBANK, and GRASIM. With low beta, medium volatility, positive 20d momentum, but weak 60d momentum and a bearish trend regime, ULTRACEMCO may trade as a selective quality cyclical rather than a straight commodity beta. GRASIM remains the industry anchor. MARUTI is both a graph neighbor and a useful domestic demand proxy from the same mega-cap ecosystem, helping capture improving discretionary and manufacturing sentiment. KOTAKBANK adds financial-condition and credit-cycle information, relevant because cement demand is tied to housing, project financing, and investment confidence. This set tests whether bullish sentiment is being validated by broader macro and funding conditions while retaining one strong industry link.

Sector-core with strongest transmission hypothesis: INFY, TCS, and HCLTECH. TECHM sits in Information Technology Services, and these three are the cleanest same-industry peers with the strongest persistent linkage. INFY is the highest-conviction graph neighbor and also leads both 60d and 120d rolling correlation, making it the anchor. TCS adds another high-correlation large peer with stable co-movement, while HCLTECH captures similar enterprise IT demand trends and remains a top rolling-correlation name. Given bullish tech sentiment and a high market mood index of 0.76, a pure sector basket tests whether TECHM responds mainly to broad IT rerating and peer read-throughs while recovering from its current drawdown in a sideways regime.

Graph-weighted diversified regime hypothesis: INFY, WIPRO, and LT. INFY and WIPRO preserve the direct IT-services signal, with both appearing as strong graph neighbors and same-industry peers. LT is introduced as a cross-sector macro proxy: it has positive correlation, shares the medium-volatility bucket, and can reflect enterprise capex, transformation spending, and domestic risk appetite that often feed into IT services demand. This set is intentionally more diversified than an all-IT trio. With sentiment broadly bullish toward technology but TECHM still in a sideways regime and down from prior highs, LT can help capture whether the next move is driven not only by IT peer momentum but also by broader cyclical participation in the market.

Risk-appetite and regime-mix hypothesis: INFY, HEROMOTOCO, and HDFCLIFE. INFY remains the essential anchor due to its dominant graph weight and strong rolling correlations with TECHM. HEROMOTOCO contributes a non-IT signal from the graph-neighbor set and shares the sideways trend regime, making it a proxy for domestic cyclical risk appetite. HDFCLIFE adds a medium-volatility financial/defensive growth component from the same market-cap and volatility neighborhood, testing whether TECHM’s forecast improves when broader quality-market participation is incorporated instead of only sector peers. Under bullish market mood, this basket explores whether TECHM benefits from a wider rotation into stable, quality names rather than a narrow IT-only move.

Staples peer transmission set. Use BRITANNIA, TATACONSUM, and HINDUNILVR to test whether ITC’s next move is best explained by consumer-defensive readthrough rather than by broader macro proxies. This is supported by same-sector membership for all three, strong static correlation for BRITANNIA and TATACONSUM (~0.32 each), graph-neighbor strength for BRITANNIA (0.529) and TATACONSUM (0.528), and elevated 60d correlation for HINDUNILVR (0.550). With bearish news focused on tobacco regulation, excise risk, and broker downgrades, this basket checks whether negative tobacco headlines spill over only partially and ITC reverts toward staples-relative behavior. It also fits ITC’s very-low volatility and sideways regime, making defensive consumer peers a clean hypothesis.

Policy-sensitive defensive yield set. Use ONGC, POWERGRID, and COALINDIA to model ITC as a mega-cap, low-volatility, dividend/yield-sensitive defensive rather than a pure consumption stock. ONGC and POWERGRID are direct graph neighbors (0.4 each), and all three share defensive/income-oriented positioning that can matter when market mood is weak (0.28) and foreign investor trimming is a concern. Given the bearish sentiment around tax and excise changes, this set tests whether ITC trades alongside policy-exposed, state-influenced cash-flow names where regulation, yield support, and macro defensiveness dominate stock behavior. This also extends a previously decent-performing motif built around COALINDIA/ONGC/POWERGRID while keeping the hypothesis economically coherent.

Liquidity and institutional-flow cross-signal set. Use KOTAKBANK, RELIANCE, and HINDUNILVR to capture three distinct drivers: KOTAKBANK for the strongest recent rolling correlation signal (60d corr ~0.603), RELIANCE for broad mega-cap macro and institutional allocation effects, and HINDUNILVR for defensive FMCG readthrough. Under current bearish mood and headlines about valuation pressure and investor selling, this set tests whether ITC’s forecast is driven by cross-sector institutional rotation: banking for liquidity/risk appetite, RELIANCE for market beta and large-cap flow anchor, and HINDUNILVR for consumption defensiveness. This is intentionally more diversified than a pure sector basket and incorporates both graph/correlation evidence and sentiment-driven flow dynamics.

Auto-demand plus financing confirmation hypothesis: use direct industry read-throughs and a credit-sensitive proxy to test whether TMCV’s bullish post-listing move is supported by durable commercial vehicle demand rather than one-off listing enthusiasm. EICHERMOT is attractive because it is both a same-industry peer and a strong relationship node for TMCV, with very high 60d rolling correlation (~0.79) and solid graph linkage (~0.62). M&M adds broader domestic auto and utility/CV cycle exposure, while SHRIRAMFIN contributes a financing and fleet-purchase signal with one of the strongest static correlations (~0.67) and graph support (~0.67). This basket leans into the very bullish sentiment and high market mood by asking whether positive news can persist only if both auto demand and vehicle-credit conditions confirm.

Cross-sector risk-on rerating hypothesis: test whether TMCV is trading less like a pure auto name and more like a large-cap high-beta cyclical beneficiary of improving domestic demand and investor risk appetite. ETERNAL is the strongest graph neighbor (~0.77), making it a key latent sentiment/flow proxy. INDIGO is another meaningful graph neighbor (~0.61) and captures discretionary mobility and domestic economic confidence. BAJAJFINSV adds a financial-conditions and wealth-effect channel, with strong static correlation (~0.62) and similar large-cap/high-volatility characteristics. Given bullish headlines, positive broker commentary, and a market mood index of 0.86, this set tests whether TMCV’s near-term forecast is best explained by broad cyclical rerating and liquidity-driven participation across discretionary and financials.

Pure peer convergence and sector re-rating hypothesis: focus on same-industry comparables to see whether TMCV’s price path is being driven by auto-sector fundamentals such as margin expansion, volume recovery, and valuation normalization. MARUTI and BAJAJ-AUTO provide large, liquid auto benchmarks with different end-market mixes, while TMPV is especially relevant as a closely related auto/Group-specific comparator in the same industry list and same sideways trend regime. This trio is less about broad market beta and more about whether the overwhelmingly bullish sentiment around TMCV should translate into synchronized sector behavior. In a sideways broader regime but with strong recent sentiment and positive 20d momentum, this basket tests whether TMCV follows industry peer confirmation rather than idiosyncratic listing effects.

Sector-core bullish continuation basket. Use SHRIRAMFIN, SBILIFE, and BAJFINANCE because they are all close financial peers to JIOFIN and each is already a graph neighbor, giving this set both economic relevance and network support. SHRIRAMFIN has the strongest graph weight, while SBILIFE and BAJFINANCE add diversified financial-services exposure across lending/insurance/retail finance. This directly matches the strongly bullish news backdrop and high market mood index, testing whether positive analyst tone and risk-on flows transmit through financial-sector leadership into JIOFIN. It also builds on the prior successful pattern where SHRIRAMFIN and SBILIFE helped produce the best historical MAE.

Correlation-led macro liquidity basket. Use ADANIPORTS, ADANIENT, and RELIANCE to capture the idea that JIOFIN is trading less like a narrow asset-management stock and more like a large-cap market-flow beneficiary. ADANIPORTS and ADANIENT have the strongest recent rolling correlations, while RELIANCE adds ecosystem adjacency and appears in the same sideways trend regime. With 20-day momentum positive, relative strength supportive, and sentiment decisively bullish, this basket tests whether JIOFIN follows broad risk-on/liquidity impulses rather than pure sector fundamentals. It is intentionally different from the sector basket by emphasizing current co-movement and market narrative transmission.

Regime-matched mixed leadership basket. Use TMCV, TRENT, and AXISBANK to combine one high-conviction graph neighbor with two large-cap regime analogs. TMCV is a strong graph-linked name and also featured in the best prior successful JIOFIN experiment, making it a high-information anchor. TRENT contributes momentum/volatility-regime similarity and captures discretionary risk appetite, while AXISBANK adds a same-sector banking signal within the same sideways regime. This set tests whether JIOFIN responds to a blend of bullish retail mood, large-cap accumulation, and financial-system beta during a sideways-but-recovering phase after a deep drawdown.

Materials-demand plus graph-core hypothesis: use GRASIM and HINDALCO from the strongest graph-neighbor cluster, then add ULTRACEMCO as a construction/housing demand proxy with strong recent co-movement. ASIANPAINT sits in a sideways regime with mixed news and only moderate market mood, so upstream materials and downstream building demand may carry more signal than stock-specific headlines. This set also aligns with the best prior successful configuration, making it a robust benchmark experiment.

Recent correlation/regime hypothesis: pair INDIGO and BAJAJFINSV, which have the strongest rolling 60d correlations, with EICHERMOT as a same-volatility-bucket and same-trend-regime name. The idea is that in a neutral-to-mixed sentiment backdrop, ASIANPAINT may trade more with flow and market structure than with pure sector fundamentals. This basket intentionally diversifies away from basic materials while preserving regime similarity and recent co-movement strength.

Consumer-defense and cross-sector read-through hypothesis: combine HINDUNILVR and NESTLEIND as defensive consumption proxies with TMPV as a top static correlated name and same-volatility-regime bridge. Mixed headlines for ASIANPAINT include both price hikes and delayed demand recovery commentary, so staples can help capture discretionary-to-essentials rotation and household demand health, while TMPV adds a market-structure linkage. This is a softer-demand lens rather than a commodity-cost lens, giving a deliberately different forecast signal.

Defensive FMCG peer-lead hypothesis: NESTLEIND and BRITANNIA are the cleanest consumption-staples comparables, with NESTLEIND the strongest graph/correlation neighbor and BRITANNIA a solid same-sector correlated peer. Add ITC to broaden staples demand exposure without leaving the defensive consumer bucket. This set tests whether HINDUNILVR’s neutral-to-mixed news flow is best explained by sector-internal rotation after earnings, where valuation caution pressures the stock short term but stable demand and dividend/acquisition support keep it tied to the staples basket. It fits the low-beta, low-volatility, sideways-regime profile and leans into market mood that is not bearish, just selective.

Defensive basket plus successful low-volatility cross-signal: TATACONSUM and ITC both map well to household consumption and staples wallet share, while SUNPHARMA adds a proven past-successful defensive neighbor and shares the low-volatility quality profile. This is intentionally similar to the best prior result structure, but swaps the exact mix toward a broader defensive rotation lens rather than pure FMCG clustering. With sentiment mixed and market mood modestly positive, this set tests whether HINDUNILVR trades with a wider ‘safe compounders’ basket instead of only direct category peers, especially during post-results digestion and sideways market action.

Macro flow and consumer wallet transmission hypothesis: NESTLEIND anchors the model with the strongest graph-supported defensive peer signal, RELIANCE captures broad consumption and index-level liquidity effects, and ICICIBANK adds consumer credit and market-risk appetite transmission. This diversified set is useful because recent headlines are mixed rather than decisively positive, suggesting HINDUNILVR may respond to broader institutional flow and household demand conditions more than stock-specific news alone. It also explicitly incorporates graph structure, using NESTLEIND plus two graph neighbors, to test whether short-term pressure is driven by market-wide positioning rather than only FMCG peer moves.

Affluent discretionary demand basket: MARUTI, TRENT, and BAJAJ-AUTO combine with TITAN through domestic premium consumption sensitivity. MARUTI and BAJAJ-AUTO are also strong graph/regime neighbors for TITAN, while TRENT adds a cleaner retail-spend proxy. This set tests whether the mixed-but-slightly-positive sentiment is enough to keep premium discretionary demand resilient despite Titan-related downgrade noise. TITAN already shows bullish regime, positive 20d/60d momentum, low beta, and strong relative strength vs Nifty, so if these consumer names remain firm, the negative headlines are more likely idiosyncratic than a broad consumption slowdown.

Correlation and stability confirmation set: TMPV, TMCV, and ULTRACEMCO emphasize TITAN's strongest graph/correlation structure. TMPV and TMCV are the two most important explicit graph neighbors, while ULTRACEMCO is one of the highest rolling-correlation names over both 60d and 120d windows and sits in the same market-cap/volatility neighborhood. This hypothesis checks whether TITAN's bullish technical regime is being driven by durable macro/cyclical factors rather than noisy headline sentiment. With market mood near neutral (0.53), persistence in these correlated peers would support continuation rather than reversal.

Cross-sector liquidity and wealth-effect signal: BAJAJFINSV, KOTAKBANK, and BAJFINANCE are chosen to capture financing conditions, urban liquidity, and consumer balance-sheet health that can feed into jewelry and luxury purchases. This is especially relevant because TITAN's direct news flow is mixed and somewhat contaminated by unrelated 'Titan' headlines, so external demand signals may be more informative than headline sentiment alone. BAJAJFINSV has prior success with TITAN, BAJFINANCE adds retail credit transmission, and KOTAKBANK captures affluent banking/liquidity trends. If financials stay constructive while TITAN weakens, that would argue for temporary stock-specific pressure rather than collapsing discretionary demand.

Auto-core with sentiment confirmation. Use MARUTI, TMCV, and HEROMOTOCO. This is the highest-conviction peer basket because EICHERMOT has bullish news flow, strong 20d momentum, and very high relative strength vs Nifty, so a same-industry confirmation set is appropriate. MARUTI, TMCV, and HEROMOTOCO are all graph neighbors or close sector peers, with MARUTI/TMCV also showing the strongest rolling correlations. The hypothesis is that EICHERMOT’s move is being driven by a broad auto demand and rerating cycle rather than idiosyncratic noise; if premium motorcycle optimism is real, it should co-move with passenger vehicles and commercial vehicle sentiment through this trio. This set leans into the positive market mood index of 0.83 and tests whether sector breadth best explains the forecast.

Balanced auto plus financing transmission. Use M&M, BAJAJFINSV, and HEROMOTOCO. M&M and HEROMOTOCO are strong graph-linked and industry-relevant names, while BAJAJFINSV adds a cross-sector but economically meaningful signal: financing availability, retail risk appetite, and discretionary purchasing power. For a low-beta, medium-volatility, sideways-regime stock with bullish headlines, this basket tests whether EICHERMOT’s upside is being supported by both vehicle demand and the credit/sentiment channel. It also stays close to past successful structures that used M&M and HEROMOTOCO effectively, but changes the third leg to explicitly capture financial conditions during a positive rerating phase.

Consumer discretionary spillover with one auto anchor. Use MARUTI, TRENT, and TITAN. EICHERMOT sits in Consumer Cyclical and current news sentiment suggests premium demand optimism, analyst confidence, and strong price momentum. MARUTI serves as the auto anchor and top graph/correlation neighbor, while TRENT and TITAN act as broader consumption and premium-spending proxies. This diversified hypothesis tests whether EICHERMOT’s forecast is better explained by a wider wealth-effect and discretionary spending upswing rather than a pure auto-factor model. It is especially relevant given the sideways trend regime: when price structure is not fully trending, cross-category confirmation from premium consumption names can improve signal robustness.

Pure materials transmission hypothesis: use the strongest structurally linked names to capture sector flow, input-cycle, and construction demand read-throughs while sentiment is mixed/slightly negative and GRASIM remains in a sideways, low-volatility regime. ULTRACEMCO is the cleanest same-industry anchor and has the strongest rolling correlation support; HINDALCO and JSWSTEEL are the heaviest graph neighbors and same-sector large caps that proxy broad basic-materials risk appetite. This set tests whether GRASIM is primarily responding to internal materials-complex dynamics rather than stock-specific paints headlines.

Downstream building-materials and headline-spillover hypothesis: combine ULTRACEMCO for core cement/building-material demand, ASIANPAINT for direct paints-adjacent sentiment spillover given recent cautious headlines, and TATASTEEL as a graph-backed cyclical construction-input signal. With market mood only 0.45 and semantic sentiment mixed, this basket is designed to capture whether GRASIM’s short-term rebound is being shaped by valuation reassessment and ecosystem sentiment across housing, renovation, and construction rather than broad market beta alone.

Cross-sector regime and allocation hypothesis: pair ULTRACEMCO as the industry anchor with SBILIFE and WIPRO to capture low-beta large-cap capital rotation, defensive quality preference, and broad domestic risk sentiment in a sideways market. GRASIM has low beta and low 30d volatility, so if mixed headlines are muting pure sector signals, its movement may align more with institutional allocation across stable large caps than with commodity beta. This set intentionally diversifies away from all-materials neighbors while retaining one strong graph/correlation anchor.

Premium discretionary + graph anchor hypothesis. TRENT’s news tone is neutral/mixed, with supportive company-specific items like dividend/bonus issue and relative strength offset by declines and insider-selling noise. Given strong 20d momentum, strong relative strength vs Nifty, but a broader sideways regime and deep drawdown, a premium-consumption basket may work best if it also includes a network-confirmed anchor. TITAN is the cleanest premium discretionary read-through and has already appeared in one of the better prior TRENT setups. M&M adds broader consumer confidence and discretionary-spend sensitivity. TMCV is the strongest graph neighbor and also one of the top static correlations, helping stabilize the basket with market-structure linkage rather than pure theme exposure.

Correlation-rotation / cross-sector macro hypothesis. TRENT’s rolling correlations suggest it may currently be trading less like a pure apparel retailer and more like a broader large-cap risk asset. With market mood mildly constructive at 0.56 but headlines mixed, this set tests whether recent co-movement and macro confirmation dominate sector intuition. INDIGO has the strongest 60d and 120d rolling correlation, making it the clearest recent co-movement proxy. GRASIM is also among the strongest recent rolling-corr names and shares the sideways trend regime. JIOFIN is a graph neighbor and same high-volatility bucket proxy for domestic risk appetite and liquidity-sensitive participation. This basket explicitly blends rolling-correlation evidence with graph structure.

Risk-regime / graph-led high-volatility hypothesis. TRENT has high 30d volatility, low beta, a large current drawdown, and a sideways trend regime, which can favor flow-based and network-linked neighbors over direct business similarity. Because the sentiment backdrop is mixed rather than decisively bullish, this basket tests whether TRENT’s next move is better explained by volatility clustering and graph connectivity. ETERNAL and TMCV are both highest-weight graph neighbors, giving strong structural links. EICHERMOT adds another graph-linked/top-correlated cyclical name and reinforces the idea that TRENT may be responding to broad consumer-cyclical risk flows rather than only apparel-specific signals. This is the most market-structure-driven of the three sets.

Auto demand + closest peer transmission hypothesis. Use HEROMOTOCO and M&M as high-confidence auto read-throughs because both are among BAJAJ-AUTO’s strongest rolling correlations (60d corr ~0.72 and ~0.77 respectively), and HEROMOTOCO is also a graph neighbor. Add MARUTI as another graph neighbor and major same-industry auto bellwether to capture broader passenger vehicle and export-cycle sentiment. This set leans into the current bullish regime, positive earnings/news flow, and strong relative strength; if the auto complex continues to confirm the breakout, BAJAJ-AUTO’s move is more likely to persist. It is a diversified intra-auto basket spanning two-wheelers, SUVs/tractors, and passenger vehicles rather than only direct two-wheeler peers.

Two-wheeler and mobility value-chain confirmation hypothesis. HEROMOTOCO remains the anchor because it is both a graph neighbor and a successful past signal for BAJAJ-AUTO. Pair it with EICHERMOT, which was part of the best prior experiment and offers premium motorcycle/export sensitivity, and TMCV, which adds commercial vehicle and mobility-cycle information. This basket tests whether bullish sentiment is fundamentally tied to vehicle demand, margin resilience, and export optimism rather than just large-cap market beta. It also closely matches the strongest historical setup for BAJAJ-AUTO, while still being distinct by emphasizing transmission across two-wheeler and broader mobility subsegments.

Cross-sector risk-on and quality-flow hypothesis. Use BEL as a graph neighbor and quality large-cap proxy, TITAN as a premium consumption/discretionary demand indicator, and TRENT as a domestic consumption momentum leader. BAJAJ-AUTO’s sentiment backdrop is bullish, with positive broker revisions and buyback support, but some of the move may also be driven by institutional rotation into low-volatility, high-quality leaders in a risk-on tape. This set is intentionally different from pure auto peers: if BEL/TITAN/TRENT stay strong alongside BAJAJ-AUTO, it suggests the stock is benefiting from broader market mood (0.76) and consumption leadership, not only auto-specific earnings momentum.

Graph-plus-NBFC leadership hypothesis: use TMCV, JIOFIN, and BAJFINANCE. TMCV is the strongest graph/correlation anchor and likely transmits vehicle-finance and retail-credit demand signals most directly into SHRIRAMFIN. JIOFIN is also a strong graph neighbor and already appeared in the best prior runs, making it a useful sentiment-sensitive fintech/retail-credit proxy. BAJFINANCE adds same-industry NBFC read-through and shared high-volatility behavior, which matters because SHRIRAMFIN has bullish news flow, positive 20d momentum, but a sideways broader regime. This basket tests whether constructive market mood (0.76) and positive earnings/dividend headlines convert into continued leadership across specialized lenders before a full trend breakout.

Banking transmission and funding-conditions hypothesis: use AXISBANK, SBIN, and TMCV. SHRIRAMFIN’s 60d/120d rolling correlations point to strong linkage with large financials, and AXISBANK/SBIN provide liquid banking-system signals for credit appetite, deposit/funding conditions, and risk sentiment. TMCV remains the required specialist finance anchor from the graph and top historical correlation list. With sentiment broadly bullish but some residual concern about charts and growth durability, this set tests whether SHRIRAMFIN is better forecast through a combination of banking beta plus vehicle-finance sensitivity rather than pure NBFC peers.

Diversified cross-sector macro-demand hypothesis: use TMCV, LT, and INDIGO. TMCV anchors the graph and auto/vehicle-finance channel. LT contributes a capex and infrastructure proxy that can reflect commercial activity, freight movement, and borrower business confidence. INDIGO adds travel/mobility demand and consumer activity exposure, offering a broader real-economy signal outside financials. This is intentionally more diverse for a stock in a sideways regime with strong short-term momentum but weak 60d momentum: if bullish headlines are signaling an economic re-acceleration rather than only sector-specific optimism, SHRIRAMFIN may respond to these cross-sector demand indicators earlier than to financial peers alone.

Healthcare leadership + sentiment transmission. Use APOLLOHOSP as the core anchor because it is the only same-industry peer, the strongest graph neighbor (0.72), and has the highest rolling correlation over both 60d and 120d windows. Add CIPLA for same-sector, same market-cap/very-low-volatility defensive healthcare confirmation, and TMPV for contemporaneous correlation support as the top overall correlated name. This tests whether bullish MAXHEALTH news flow and constructive market mood (0.72) propagate through healthcare leaders and close co-movers even while MAXHEALTH remains in a bearish trend regime and deep drawdown.

Defensive low-volatility recovery basket. Use BRITANNIA and TATACONSUM as consumption-defensive proxies that also appear in past successful MAXHEALTH sets and share the same low-volatility/market-cap style profile. Add CIPLA to retain healthcare-defensive information and graph connectivity. This hypothesis targets MAXHEALTH’s unusual combination of bullish sentiment, positive relative strength vs Nifty, very low beta, and bearish trend regime: if the stock is being accumulated as a defensive compounder rather than purely on hospital-sector news, this basket should forecast recovery better than pure sector peers.

Quality rotation with sector confirmation. Use APOLLOHOSP for direct same-industry signal and graph strength, SUNPHARMA for broader healthcare sentiment spillover, and HDFCLIFE as a low-beta institutional quality cross-sector proxy from the same market-cap bucket. This set is deliberately more diverse: it tests whether bullish market mood is driving allocation toward stable, high-quality defensive franchises across healthcare and financial protection, with APOLLOHOSP validating industry-specific moves and SUNPHARMA/HDFCLIFE capturing broader defensive rotation while MAXHEALTH remains technically bearish.

Private-bank core with idiosyncratic stress isolation. Use SBIN, HDFCBANK, and AXISBANK.
