This set leans into the 0.82 market mood, bullish trend regime, positive momentum, and the idea that deal optimism spills first into pharma peers and then into adjacent healthcare leaders.

Defensive ultra-mega-cap liquidity regime hypothesis. Use TCS, ICICIBANK, and HINDUNILVR from the graph-neighbor/mega-cap cluster to test whether SUNPHARMA’s move is being driven less by pharma-specific fundamentals and more by broad institutional allocation into low-beta, low-volatility, quality large caps. This is especially relevant because SUNPHARMA itself has very low beta, low 30-day volatility, ultra-mega market cap status, and a bullish trend regime. Positive news may attract incremental flows from the same defensive-quality buyer base that supports these graph-linked names.

Hybrid sector-plus-market structure hypothesis. Use CIPLA and DIVISLAB for pharma/healthcare manufacturing read-through, then add RELIANCE as a graph neighbor to anchor broader market liquidity and risk appetite. CIPLA provides the strongest peer linkage, DIVISLAB adds same-industry diversification with meaningful rolling correlation, and RELIANCE helps detect whether SUNPHARMA’s post-news strength is amplified by broad large-cap risk-on conditions rather than only sector sentiment. This basket is useful when sentiment is strongly bullish and the target is already near highs with only shallow current drawdown, since it separates stock-specific M&A rerating from general market sponsorship.

Auto-core plus graph-strength hypothesis: use the strongest structural peers to model HEROMOTOCO in a sideways regime with mixed but not bearish sentiment. M&M and MARUTI are both high-conviction graph/industry neighbors, while BAJAJ-AUTO is a direct two-wheeler peer and top long-horizon correlated name. This basket stays close to the underlying auto demand signal and should work if recent news around earnings quality, demand stabilisation, and EV progress causes HEROMOTOCO to trade with the broader listed auto complex rather than on idiosyncratic headlines. The neutral-to-slightly constructive market mood (0.53) supports using high-beta-to-industry relationships without reaching too far into defensive proxies.

Regime-diversified mobility hypothesis: combine TMPV, EICHERMOT, and TMCV. TMPV is the top graph neighbor and shares market-cap/volatility characteristics; EICHERMOT has very strong rolling correlation and captures premium motorcycle demand; TMCV adds commercial-vehicle and capex-cycle exposure. Given HEROMOTOCO's sideways trend, weak 60-day momentum, and mixed news flow, this set tests whether the stock is better explained by broader mobility and vehicle-demand normalization across subsegments instead of only mass two-wheeler trends. This also adds diversification versus prior pure passenger-vehicle combinations while still staying inside the auto/manufacturing ecosystem.

Cross-sector consumer-finance resilience hypothesis: use TITAN, HDFCLIFE, and INDUSINDBK. Hero MotoCorp sits in consumer cyclical, and the news mix suggests neither a clean bullish nor bearish read; in that setting, broader household confidence, financing availability, and discretionary spending may matter more than tight auto-peer mapping. TITAN captures premium discretionary consumption, HDFCLIFE reflects retail savings/protection behavior and financial confidence, and INDUSINDBK is a credit transmission proxy relevant for vehicle financing. This set intentionally departs from auto peers to test whether a neutral market mood and sideways price action make HEROMOTOCO respond more to consumption and financing conditions than to sector-specific co-movement. It is also informed by a past successful diversification pattern using HDFCLIFE and TITAN.

Sector-pure momentum continuation: TATASTEEL, JSWSTEEL, and GRASIM. This is the highest-conviction materials cluster built around the strongest graph neighbors and the clearest industrial read-through. TATASTEEL has the highest graph weight and strongest long-horizon correlation, JSWSTEEL is both a top historical and rolling correlated peer in the same bullish trend and low-volatility regime, and GRASIM adds another strong graph-linked basic-materials large-cap. With HINDALCO showing bullish news sentiment, strong 20-day momentum, high relative strength vs Nifty, and only a shallow current drawdown, this set tests whether the current move is a broad basic-materials upcycle and earnings-led continuation rather than idiosyncratic stock-specific strength. It is also close to previously successful configurations, but swaps in GRASIM to capture diversified materials demand.

Commodity-chain macro confirmation: TATASTEEL, COALINDIA, and ONGC. This hypothesis focuses on whether HINDALCO's rally is being driven by a broader commodity and input-cost regime. TATASTEEL remains the anchor because of its dominant graph weight and persistent correlation. COALINDIA and ONGC extend the signal into fuel and energy, which matter for aluminum economics and often co-move during commodity upcycles. Given the strongly bullish news flow and market mood index of 0.83, this trio tests if optimism is supported by macro resource strength rather than only result-season excitement. This set also has precedent in past successful runs, making it a robust alternative to pure sector clustering while still remaining economically linked.

Cross-sector risk-on large-cap signal: TATASTEEL, SBILIFE, and NESTLEIND. This is a diversification hypothesis designed to separate commodity-specific momentum from broader institutional rotation into stable, large-cap, lower-volatility names. TATASTEEL preserves the core industrial signal and strongest graph connection. SBILIFE shares the large-cap bucket, low-volatility regime, and bullish trend characteristics with HINDALCO, while NESTLEIND adds a defensive consumer staple with similar regime traits but low direct industry overlap. In a strongly positive sentiment backdrop, if HINDALCO continues to track both a cyclical metal leader and defensive quality large-caps, that would imply the rally is part of a broader market-wide risk-on allocation rather than a narrow aluminum/metal event. This set is also informed by past success using TATASTEEL plus defensive cross-sector names.

Correlation-led discretionary basket: INDIGO, M&M, and TITAN. This extends the strongest prior successful pattern around INDIGO/TITAN while swapping in M&M as the most relevant graph-and-industry anchor. INDIGO has the strongest 60d rolling correlation and may capture mobility/travel-demand sentiment that spills into auto names when macro risk eases. M&M is a top graph neighbor and same-industry peer, giving direct auto-demand read-through. TITAN adds broader premium-consumption tone, useful because news sentiment is mixed: short-term geopolitical de-escalation supports risk appetite and discretionary spending expectations, but weak trailing performance and profit-taking concerns argue against using only pure auto peers. With TMPV in a sideways regime but positive 20d momentum, this set tests whether near-term upside is being transmitted through consumer-risk-on channels rather than solely stock-specific factors.

Pure auto + financing sensitivity hypothesis: HEROMOTOCO, M&M, and SHRIRAMFIN. This is a cleaner sector/industry framework for TMPV as an auto manufacturer facing mixed headlines. M&M and HEROMOTOCO are both same-industry names, and M&M is also a strong graph neighbor with high observed linkage. SHRIRAMFIN adds a vehicle-financing and credit-cycle proxy, which matters when demand expectations may improve on calmer macro conditions but investors remain cautious due to post-demerger pressure and historical underperformance concerns. Given neutral overall sentiment and only moderately positive market mood, this trio tests whether TMPV’s next move is better explained by underlying auto demand plus financing conditions than by broader discretionary proxies.

Regime-balanced industrial-consumption hybrid: LT, ULTRACEMCO, and MARUTI. LT and ULTRACEMCO are both top correlated/graph-linked names and share TMPV’s medium-volatility style characteristics, making them useful non-auto market-structure anchors. MARUTI adds a direct same-industry passenger-vehicle benchmark. This set is intentionally more cross-sector and macro-sensitive: LT and ULTRACEMCO can capture domestic investment/cyclical sentiment, while MARUTI preserves auto-demand relevance. That is attractive under the current backdrop of mixed headlines, where a ceasefire/de-escalation impulse may lift broader cyclical sentiment even if TMPV-specific narratives remain noisy. In a sideways trend regime, this basket tests whether TMPV is trading more like a broad cyclical-consumer name than as a pure standalone auto story.

Hypothesis 1 — Core private-bank transmission set. Use HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, and SBIN. AXISBANK is in a sideways regime with mixed/neutral news: modest profit growth is offset by margin-pressure commentary and weak market tone, so the cleanest signal may come from direct banking peers rather than idiosyncratic headlines. HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, and SBIN are all strong graph neighbors, and ICICIBANK/SBIN are among the top correlated names. This basket captures private-bank and system-level banking beta: deposit competition, NIM compression, loan growth expectations, and sector re-rating. Including SBIN adds a public-sector banking read-through that can help distinguish whether AXISBANK moves are private-bank specific or part of a broader banking cycle.

Hypothesis 2 — Financial-beta and retail-credit stress set. Use BAJAJFINSV, SHRIRAMFIN, and HDFCBANK. In a mixed earnings/news backdrop with neutral sentiment and a 0.5 market mood, AXISBANK may trade more on broader financial conditions than on standalone fundamentals. BAJAJFINSV and SHRIRAMFIN have very high rolling 60-day correlations with AXISBANK, making them strong candidates for capturing shifts in credit demand, retail financing appetite, and valuation compression across lenders. HDFCBANK serves as the graph-linked bank anchor to stabilize the signal and keep the basket tied to core banking conditions. This set tests whether AXISBANK is currently responding to cross-financial risk appetite rather than only same-industry peer moves.

Hypothesis 3 — Cross-sector demand and financed-consumption regime set. Use HDFCBANK, MARUTI, and TITAN. With AXISBANK showing positive 20-day momentum but negative 60-day momentum, the stock appears to be in a recovery-inside-sideways regime. In that environment, financed consumption and discretionary demand can provide useful leading information for retail-credit-sensitive banks. HDFCBANK is the banking anchor and strongest graph neighbor; MARUTI is also a graph neighbor and reflects auto-finance demand, while TITAN represents discretionary spending confidence. Mixed sentiment around AXISBANK suggests stock-specific news is not decisive, so broader household spending and financing signals may improve forecasts versus a pure peer basket.

Sector-core + construction spillover hypothesis: Use the strongest graph/correlation structure around JSWSTEEL while leaning into the bullish trend regime and positive news tone. TATASTEEL is the closest same-industry anchor with the highest graph weight and strongest rolling correlation, making it the cleanest steel beta signal. HINDALCO adds metals-cycle breadth and shares the low-volatility, bullish-regime profile. ULTRACEMCO contributes downstream construction/infrastructure demand sensitivity and has very strong rolling correlations with JSWSTEEL. With sentiment bullish but not euphoric, this set tests whether near-term forecasting is best driven by direct sector leadership plus end-demand from the building cycle.

Infrastructure demand transmission hypothesis: Recent positive mood, fundraising/dividend/JV headlines, and strong momentum suggest JSWSTEEL may be trading as a capex and industrial activity beneficiary rather than only as a steel peer. ADANIPORTS captures logistics throughput and trade flow, COALINDIA reflects industrial fuel/input-cycle strength, and GRASIM adds building-materials/infrastructure exposure while also being a strong graph and rolling-correlation neighbor. This is a diversified but still economically linked basket designed to detect whether steel demand expectations are being pulled by the broader infrastructure ecosystem under a constructive market mood index of 0.67.

Low-vol bullish macro-rotation hypothesis: JSWSTEEL itself has low beta, low recent volatility, positive 20d momentum, and sits in a bullish regime, so part of its short-horizon behavior may reflect large-cap cyclical risk appetite rather than pure commodity linkage. BAJAJ-AUTO is also a graph neighbor and shares the low-vol bullish profile, POWERGRID captures domestic capex/utility stability, and NTPC adds power-demand and industrial activity confirmation. This set intentionally reduces direct metals exposure to test whether forecast accuracy improves when JSWSTEEL is modeled as a low-vol mega-cap beneficiary of improving macro sentiment and domestic growth rotation.

Private-bank core with one public-bank breadth anchor: AXISBANK, HDFCBANK, and SBIN. This is the cleanest industry-transmission hypothesis for INDUSINDBK, using same-industry peers to capture deposit growth, funding-cost/NIM pressure, credit quality, and RBI/regulatory spillovers. It fits the current setup well: news sentiment is neutral-to-mixed with a slight positive tilt, market mood is mildly constructive at 0.54, and INDUSINDBK is in a bullish regime with strong 20d momentum after a very deep 1y drawdown. AXISBANK is especially useful because it has already appeared repeatedly in prior successful INDUSINDBK runs and is a closer operating-beta peer. HDFCBANK adds sector leadership and balance-sheet quality, helping distinguish durable recovery from short-covering. SBIN broadens the signal to system-wide banking sentiment and credit-cycle direction. This set intentionally leans away from graph-diversification and instead tests whether the best forecast still comes from the most direct banking comparables, consistent with the best historical result that used a pure bank basket.

Graph-aware financials basket: BAJFINANCE, JIOFIN, and SHRIRAMFIN. This hypothesis emphasizes the graph neighbors and broader financial-risk network around INDUSINDBK rather than only same-industry banks. All three are either explicit graph neighbors or close same-sector financial transmission names, and they can capture retail credit demand, unsecured lending appetite, funding conditions, cross-holding sentiment, and market-wide financial risk-on/risk-off behavior. This is relevant because headlines are mixed: there is some operational/share-price support, but also pressure from investor-return weakness and regulatory/shareholding concerns. In that environment, INDUSINDBK may trade less on pure bank fundamentals and more on the broader financial complex. BAJFINANCE and SHRIRAMFIN add high-beta credit-cycle sensitivity, while JIOFIN reflects financial-market mood and retail participation dynamics. The set also matches the stock’s high-volatility profile better than a pure quality-bank basket.

Hybrid confirmation basket with one bank, one correlation proxy, and one defensive regime check: AXISBANK, TMPV, and DRREDDY. This is a more diversified hypothesis designed to test whether INDUSINDBK’s recent strength is a genuine regime move or a fragile rebound. AXISBANK remains the essential same-industry anchor. TMPV is included because it is the top overall correlation name and also in the same market-cap bucket, making it a useful statistical co-movement proxy even if not sector-linked. DRREDDY, from the bullish trend-regime cohort, acts as a defensive cross-sector control: if INDUSINDBK continues to perform when a defensive leader also confirms market stability, the rally may be more robust; if signals diverge, it may indicate stock-specific noise. This structure explicitly incorporates the slightly positive but mixed sentiment backdrop and the moderate market mood, where both direct peer read-through and cross-sector confirmation matter. It also creates diversity versus the historical bank-heavy experiments while still retaining one proven banking neighbor.

Hypothesis 1 - Policy-sensitive PSU yield basket. ONGC’s current setup is dominated by strongly bullish news sentiment tied to a government royalty cut, so the cleanest test is whether the move is being transmitted through policy-sensitive, state-linked, dividend-oriented large caps. COALINDIA and NTPC are the two strongest graph neighbors and also among the highest historical correlations, while POWERGRID matches ONGC’s very low volatility, low-beta, mega-cap defensive profile. This basket tests whether ONGC is trading as part of a broader PSU/income/regulated-earnings rerating rather than only as a crude-linked stock.

Hypothesis 2 - Energy chain plus market leader confirmation. ONGC has bullish trend, positive 20d/60d momentum, and strong relative strength, so a second hypothesis is that the rally is not just PSU-specific but part of a wider energy-and-infrastructure risk-on move. BPCL adds direct sector adjacency within Energy, RELIANCE contributes integrated energy and broad market leadership, and ADANIPORTS adds cyclical trade/logistics sensitivity in the same bullish regime. This set checks whether ONGC’s upside is reinforced by downstream energy demand and macro growth proxies under a very positive market mood index.

Hypothesis 3 - Metals/industrial cross-asset commodity signal. ONGC’s bullish sentiment may also be interacting with a broader commodities and industrial cycle rather than only company-specific news. HINDALCO and TATASTEEL are the strongest rolling correlation names over 60d/120d and share the current bullish trend regime, while BEL adds a mega-cap domestic industrial/PSU signal with stable institutional ownership characteristics. This basket tests whether ONGC behaves more like a low-volatility commodity/industrial beta expression when market mood is strongly positive, capturing cross-sector cyclical spillover beyond pure oil and gas peers.

Sector-core with one graph overlay: ONGC, RELIANCE, ADANIENT. BPCL is in a bearish longer-term regime with negative 60d momentum but a positive 20d rebound, while news is neutral/mixed rather than outright bearish. That setup favors a neighbor set anchored in direct energy transmission but with one high-beta market-structure signal. ONGC captures upstream crude sensitivity that often leads OMC margin expectations; RELIANCE is the closest same-industry refining/petrochem anchor and should reflect refining margin and policy/news spillovers; ADANIENT is both a same-sector candidate and a strong graph neighbor, useful for capturing broader commodity, policy, and risk-appetite effects when market mood is middling at 0.47. This is close to the historically best BPCL recipe, but replaces COALINDIA with a stronger graph-linked cyclical energy/infrastructure name to better reflect mixed sentiment and recent rebound behavior.

Correlation-macro basket: SBIN, NTPC, LT. BPCL’s relative strength vs Nifty is strong despite the bearish trend regime, suggesting stock behavior may be partly driven by macro and domestic-demand conditions rather than only oil-specific news. SBIN is among the top correlated names and captures system liquidity, credit pulse, and broad risk appetite; NTPC is also top correlated and adds a domestic power-demand and regulated energy signal that can proxy industrial/economic activity; LT is both top correlated over longer windows and tied to capex/infrastructure momentum, which connects to diesel demand and industrial fuel consumption. This diversified set is intentionally non-pure-energy and tests whether BPCL’s near-term path is better explained by macro consumption and investment proxies under mixed headlines and neutral market mood. It also complements prior experiments by leaning harder into cross-sector common-factor behavior.

Volatility/regime hybrid with graph support: INDUSINDBK, TECHM, TMCV. BPCL sits in a high-volatility bucket and bearish trend regime, so a useful alternative hypothesis is that market-state similarity matters more than sector identity. INDUSINDBK and TECHM are explicit graph neighbors, meaning the broader feature graph already links BPCL to them; INDUSINDBK also represents high-beta financial stress/risk-on swings, while TECHM contributes a growth/IT sentiment leg that can help detect market-wide factor rotation. TMCV belongs to the same high-volatility bucket and is one of BPCL’s strongest static correlations among candidates, so it can act as the regime-similar momentum/dispersion proxy. With sentiment mixed and mood only neutral, this basket tests whether BPCL is trading as part of a broader volatile-factor cluster rather than purely as an energy stock.

Staples defensives under headline pressure. Use BRITANNIA, TATACONSUM, and HINDUNILVR to test whether ITC trades primarily as a Consumer Defensive name despite tobacco-specific bearish news. This set is supported by strong structural similarity: all are same-sector peers, BRITANNIA and TATACONSUM are the two strongest graph neighbors (~0.53 each), and HINDUNILVR is both a top correlated name and in the same sideways regime. With sentiment bearish and mood weak (0.32), this hypothesis assumes investors rotate within low-volatility staples rather than abandoning defensives altogether; relative moves among FMCG names may explain ITC better than broader macro beta, especially given ITC’s near-zero beta and very low 30d volatility.

Institutional flow and banking-liquidity transmission. Use KOTAKBANK, AXISBANK, and RELIANCE to test whether ITC is being driven by cross-sector allocation shifts rather than only cigarette-tax headlines. KOTAKBANK is the strongest rolling-correlation link over both 60d and 120d windows and is also a graph neighbor; AXISBANK shares the same mega-cap/sideways regime profile and has worked in prior successful runs; RELIANCE adds broad macro and institutional-risk appetite signal with moderate correlation and same trend regime. Under bearish sentiment, downgrades, and policy concerns, this set captures the idea that ITC behaves like a large, low-volatility parking stock whose short-horizon moves depend on liquidity rotation across financials and benchmark-heavy mega caps.

Policy-sensitive dividend defensive basket. Use ONGC, POWERGRID, and COALINDIA to model ITC as a yield-oriented, regulation-sensitive mega-cap defensive. ONGC and POWERGRID are direct graph neighbors, while COALINDIA has already appeared in the best prior ITC experiments and fits the same mega-cap defensive income profile. This is a deliberately different hypothesis from staples or banking: with negative sentiment centered on excise, taxes, and pressure on the cigarette business, ITC may co-move more with state-influenced, cash-generative, policy-exposed names than with consumption peers. The weak market mood and very low volatility also support testing whether defensive yield cohorts explain return behavior during sideways regimes.

Auto-peer + graph-structure hypothesis. Use MARUTI, EICHERMOT, and TMPV. This is the cleanest industry-aligned set: all are direct auto/vehicle peers, and all three are strongly supported by the structure data. MARUTI is the strongest graph neighbor and also has very high rolling correlation with M&M over both 60d and 120d windows, suggesting current co-movement is especially strong. TMPV has the highest raw correlation in the metadata and is also a top graph neighbor, while EICHERMOT is another graph-backed same-industry name that can capture premium vehicle demand and shared supply-chain/sector flows. With news sentiment neutral and no M&M-specific catalyst, the forecast is more likely to be driven by sector rotation, industry demand, and shared auto-market positioning than idiosyncratic news. This set tests whether M&M is best explained by pure automobile cluster behavior in a bearish trend regime but with some short-term 20d rebound.

Cross-sector macro transmission hypothesis. Use KOTAKBANK, ADANIPORTS, and ULTRACEMCO. This basket is deliberately different from pure auto clustering and is aimed at financing, logistics/trade, and domestic investment activity. KOTAKBANK is one of the strongest 120d rolling correlations and is relevant for auto loan and commercial vehicle financing sensitivity. ADANIPORTS can proxy freight throughput, exports, and infrastructure-linked activity that affects tractors and CV demand. ULTRACEMCO shares the same bearish regime and can reflect construction/rural capex conditions, which matter for M&M's farm and utility vehicle exposure. In a neutral headline environment and mixed market mood, macro state variables may dominate over company-specific sentiment. This set tests whether M&M is currently trading more like a financing-and-capex-sensitive cyclical than like a narrow auto peer.

Consumer-cyclical + discretionary resilience hypothesis. Use TITAN, HEROMOTOCO, and BAJAJ-AUTO. TITAN is a notable graph neighbor despite not being a direct auto manufacturer, which suggests latent shared exposure to discretionary consumption and broad consumer confidence. HEROMOTOCO adds direct auto/two-wheeler sector sensitivity and is also graph-supported, while BAJAJ-AUTO strengthens the consumer vehicle demand signal from the same industry family. This is useful because M&M sits in Consumer Cyclical, not just industrial auto beta, and neutral news flow implies broader demand sentiment may matter more than headlines. Given low beta, medium volatility, bearish trend regime, and positive short-term momentum, this set tests whether M&M's near-term path is better captured by discretionary spending resilience and consumer demand proxies rather than only heavy macro or direct peer co-movement.

Sector-pure staples quality basket. Use BRITANNIA and ITC because they are the two strongest graph neighbors and have already shown up in the better prior TATACONSUM runs, suggesting persistent signal relevance. Add HINDUNILVR instead of repeating NESTLEIND to keep the basket tied to the current 60d rolling-correlation structure, where HINDUNILVR is the strongest recent co-mover. This tests whether bullish sentiment, earnings strength, analyst upgrades, and positive market mood are propagating through a defensive FMCG leadership cluster in a low-beta, very-low-volatility environment.

Correlation-led packaged-foods transmission basket. Combine BRITANNIA and NESTLEIND as same-industry packaged-food peers with solid long-window and recent correlation support, then add HINDUNILVR as the strongest 60d rolling-correlation anchor. This is a cleaner peer-expression hypothesis than using broader graph-only names: if TATACONSUM's recent momentum and positive news are being priced as a sector-wide staples rerating, these three should capture that transmission. It also fits the sideways trend regime, where relative strength versus Nifty and defensive sector rotation can matter more than broad beta.

Defensive cross-sector quality-flow basket. Keep BRITANNIA as the highest-conviction graph neighbor, then pair it with CIPLA and APOLLOHOSP from the graph/volatility buckets to test whether TATACONSUM is trading as part of a broader low-volatility institutional quality trade rather than a pure FMCG move. The bullish news backdrop, strong market mood, low beta, and very low realized volatility support a hypothesis of capital rotating into stable compounders across consumer and healthcare. This basket is deliberately diversified to capture cross-sector defensive flow signals while retaining one core consumption anchor.

Pure banking stress-propagation hypothesis: use ICICIBANK, AXISBANK, and HDFCBANK. This is the cleanest sector-similarity setup for SBIN given bearish post-earnings sentiment, weak market mood (0.31), and concern around profit miss/margin compression. ICICIBANK and AXISBANK are the two strongest graph neighbors, and both are also among the strongest correlation/industry peers; HDFCBANK adds a stable large private-bank benchmark from the same industry and market-cap cohort. In a sideways regime, this set tests whether SBIN’s recent weakness is mainly a bank-wide repricing event rather than stock-specific noise. It also builds on prior successful bank-peer experiments while adding the largest industry anchor.

Broader financial-services contagion hypothesis: use SBILIFE, BAJFINANCE, and SHRIRAMFIN. This set intentionally moves beyond pure banks to capture spillover in financial risk appetite after negative SBI headlines. SBILIFE and BAJFINANCE are both graph neighbors, while SHRIRAMFIN has the strongest rolling 60d/120d correlation profile with SBIN, suggesting useful dynamic co-movement. With bearish sentiment and low-beta/low-volatility characteristics, SBIN may trade less on market beta and more on changes in credit, lending, and financials sentiment; this basket tests whether the market is repricing the wider financial complex rather than only public/private banks.

Cross-sector macro-flow hypothesis: use ADANIPORTS, RELIANCE, and SUNPHARMA. This is a diversified regime/mood basket for a sideways market. ADANIPORTS is a top-correlated cyclical and trade/activity proxy; RELIANCE is a mega-cap market barometer from the same market-cap bucket and a strong read on index-level risk appetite; SUNPHARMA is a defensive low-volatility peer and also a graph neighbor. Given the bearish news tone but still-positive medium-term relative strength for SBIN, this set tests whether future returns are driven more by rotation between cyclicals, defensives, and broad market flows than by direct banking peers alone.

Energy-policy transmission set: [ONGC, NTPC, BEL]. This is the strongest continuation hypothesis because it aligns with both graph structure and prior success. ONGC and BEL are the top two graph neighbors, while NTPC is a persistent top correlation partner over 60d/120d and shares the bullish regime. For COALINDIA, mixed-to-mildly-positive sentiment plus a 0.58 market mood suggests a market still willing to reward stable state-linked energy names despite profit-quality concerns. ONGC captures upstream commodity and government-policy spillover, NTPC captures thermal power demand and coal offtake sensitivity, and BEL adds a high-weight graph/policy-linked defensive leg that may proxy institutional flows into low-volatility PSU names. This set tests whether near-term returns are driven by PSU/energy momentum persistence rather than pure coal-specific news.

Commodity-cycle and industrial demand set: [HINDALCO, TATASTEEL, ONGC]. This is a broader cyclical hypothesis that COALINDIA may trade with the industrial and commodity complex, not just within Energy. HINDALCO and TATASTEEL are among the top correlated names and both sit in similar bullish/cyclical regimes; ONGC anchors the basket with direct energy linkage. With COALINDIA showing positive 20d/60d momentum, strong relative strength vs Nifty, and low realized volatility, this set tests whether the stock is participating in a reflation-style basket where metal demand, energy pricing, and macro growth sentiment move together. The neutral headline tone but mildly constructive market mood supports this idea: headlines are not cleanly bullish, yet price action may continue to respond to cross-commodity risk appetite.

Defensive yield-and-rotation set: [POWERGRID, ITC, BPCL]. This is the diversification hypothesis, intentionally different from the standard graph-heavy energy basket. COALINDIA has ultra-low beta, low 30d volatility, mega-cap status, and supportive dividend sentiment; that profile can attract the same capital rotation as other defensive carry names. POWERGRID captures regulated utility/PSU yield flows, ITC captures domestic defensive cash-flow and dividend rotation, and BPCL reintroduces an energy-sector link tied to downstream fuel demand and policy sensitivity. In a mixed news backdrop with mildly positive mood, this set tests whether COALINDIA’s short-term forecast is better explained by low-volatility income-seeking allocations and quasi-defensive positioning than by pure commodity beta. BPCL also complements the graph-informed energy narrative without duplicating the exact ONGC-NTPC-BEL cluster.

Core IT stress transmission hypothesis: use TCS, TECHM, and HCLTECH. WIPRO’s news/sentiment backdrop is clearly bearish, with weak IT-sector tone, weak forward outlook, and post-earnings pressure overwhelming buyback support. In that setting, the cleanest test is whether WIPRO’s next move is mainly explained by direct sector peers under shared demand and margin pressure. This set is strongly supported by both the graph structure and correlation data: TCS is the strongest graph neighbor, while TECHM and HCLTECH are also top graph neighbors and same-industry names. It also adds diversity within IT services: TCS as large-cap bellwether, TECHM as a more cyclical peer, and HCLTECH as another large outsourced-services benchmark. Given WIPRO’s sideways regime, negative 60d momentum, and low beta, this basket tests whether downside is sector-led rather than broad market-led.

Sector-plus-enterprise-spend hypothesis: use INFY, TCS, and LT. Bearish sentiment suggests the market is pricing not only company-specific weakness but also softer tech spending. INFY and TCS capture direct IT-services readthrough and are among WIPRO’s strongest correlation/graph neighbors. LT adds a cross-sector but economically relevant signal: enterprise capex, digital transformation budgets, and large project confidence. This is useful because WIPRO’s recent weakness may be partly tied to delayed client spending and weaker corporate decision cycles, not just peer stock sympathy. Past successful runs already showed LT working well alongside IT peers for WIPRO, which increases confidence that this is a robust nonredundant feature set. This basket is suitable if you want a slightly broader macro-demand framing than pure peer modeling.

Risk-off large-cap rotation hypothesis: use INFY, GRASIM, and SBILIFE. WIPRO has low beta, low 30d volatility, a deep drawdown from prior highs, and a sideways trend regime, while market mood is weak. That combination can produce behavior where the stock trades partly as a defensive large-cap allocation vehicle rather than only as an IT name. INFY remains in the set as the essential sector anchor and strong graph/correlation neighbor. GRASIM and SBILIFE add non-IT large-cap, low-volatility, sideways-regime comparators to capture broader institutional rotation and sentiment-driven allocation under bearish conditions. Large-cap/high-volatility liquidity regime basket: use BAJAJFINSV, JIOFIN, and ULTRACEMCO. Utility-energy core leadership hypothesis: use POWERGRID, ONGC, and COALINDIA. Defensive mega-cap allocation hypothesis: use POWERGRID, KOTAKBANK, and ITC. POWERGRID anchors the sector signal via the highest graph weight, while KOTAKBANK and ITC are direct graph neighbors and belong to similarly defensive, very-low-volatility / institutional large-cap cohorts. Cross-sector capex and industrial transmission hypothesis: use JSWSTEEL, ADANIPORTS, and COALINDIA. JSWSTEEL captures cyclical capex/risk-on behavior, ADANIPORTS captures logistics and infrastructure demand transmission, and COALINDIA bridges industrial growth with power-fuel demand. Given bullish sentiment, strong relative strength vs Nifty, and a constructive market mood, this set tests whether NTPC is benefiting from macro expansion and capex-theme spillovers.

Private-bank core hypothesis: HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, and SBIN. This set leans on the strongest graph structure and direct banking transmission. Broader financial-beta hypothesis: BAJAJFINSV, SHRIRAMFIN, and HDFCBANK. Cross-sector demand and risk-appetite hypothesis: HDFCBANK, MARUTI, and TITAN. This set intentionally mixes one strong banking anchor with consumption-sensitive mega caps. Auto-correlation anchor with industry breadth. Use MARUTI, TMCV, and M&M. Premium consumption spillover hypothesis. Use TRENT, TITAN, and MARUTI. Past success suggests EICHERMOT can be forecast well not only by auto peers but also by premium discretionary names. With market mood strongly bullish and headlines pointing to analyst upgrades, momentum, and a 52-week-high type narrative, premium spending proxies may capture the same wealth-effect and aspirational-consumption impulse supporting EICHERMOT. This is useful because EICHERMOT is currently in a sideways regime, where cross-category confirmation may outperform a narrowly clustered peer set.

Cross-sector risk-on plus two-wheeler financing transmission. Use HEROMOTOCO, BAJAJFINSV, and BAJAJ-AUTO. This basket tests whether EICHERMOT’s upside is being driven less by broad auto beta and more by premium two-wheeler sentiment reinforced by consumer finance conditions and market-wide risk-on behavior.

Hypothesis 1 — Sentiment-amplified energy chain with a logistics confirmation signal. With bullish sentiment driven partly by post-earnings reaction and Jio IPO-related optimism, this basket tests whether RELIANCE near-term moves are being led more by platform/digital valuation and domestic risk appetite than by oil and refining variables. Hypothesis 3 — Low-volatility mega-cap rotation under constructive mood. Use HINDUNILVR, TCS, and ICICIBANK to model RELIANCE through institutional allocation behavior across ultra-mega, lower-volatility Indian leaders. HINDUNILVR and TCS are already graph neighbors, and ICICIBANK adds a large financial risk-on/risk-off gauge from the same market-cap cohort. Sector-cost-pass-through hypothesis: ASIANPAINT has mixed/neutral news flow, a sideways trend, moderate positive 20d momentum, and remains in drawdown, so upstream materials and construction-demand read-throughs may matter more than stock-specific headlines. The idea is to capture input-cost, commodity-cycle, and end-demand signals that influence paint margins and volume recovery.

Recent co-movement / market-structure hypothesis: In a neutral sentiment tape with market mood only modestly positive (0.56), recent flow-based leadership can dominate fundamentals. ASIANPAINT shows very high rolling 60d correlation with INDIGO, BAJAJFINSV, and ULTRACEMCO; using the first two plus EICHERMOT adds another same-volatility-bucket and same-trend-regime large-cap that can proxy discretionary/risk-on participation. This basket tests whether ASIANPAINT is currently trading more like a broad quality large-cap momentum cluster than a pure materials name.

Consumer-demand plus defensive cross-signal hypothesis: Mixed headlines mention rebound and price hikes, but also weak Q3 and demand-recovery concerns. That makes downstream consumption proxies useful. HINDUNILVR is a top correlated defensive consumption name and shares the sideways regime; NESTLEIND adds another large-cap staples signal from the same market-cap bucket; GRASIM anchors the basket with a graph/sector neighbor so the model still sees materials linkage. This set tests whether ASIANPAINT near-term returns are better explained by urban consumption resilience plus a residual materials factor, rather than by metals-heavy cyclicality alone.

Private-bank core plus broad system confirmation. INDUSINDBK has mixed/neutral news flow, mildly constructive market mood (0.55), strong 20d momentum, and a bullish regime after a deep 1y drawdown, so the first hypothesis should stay close to the cleanest transmission channel. This also aligns with prior successful INDUSINDBK runs, where pure bank baskets beat baseline. The set is intentionally conservative and tests whether recent recovery is truly bank-led rather than a broader cross-asset bounce.

Graph-financial hybrid for sentiment transmission across lending franchises. With sentiment balanced rather than strongly bullish, and volatility still high, a diversified financials basket can help detect whether INDUSINDBK is trading as part of a broader credit-risk appetite move. BAJFINANCE and SHRIRAMFIN are both same-sector names and important graph neighbors in spirit, with SHRIRAMFIN explicitly appearing in graph links and BAJFINANCE also a graph neighbor. This trio tests whether the stock’s positive price action reflects improving financial-sector risk appetite beyond traditional banks. It is a more network-aware hypothesis than a pure peer basket and may work if market mood stays constructive but stock-specific news remains mixed.

Cross-sector regime and volatility confirmation. DRREDDY adds defensive balance from the same market-cap bucket/trend-regime cohorts, helping distinguish durable recovery from fragile short covering if defensives start leading. Consumer discretionary quality basket with graph support. Recent-correlation rotation basket. Graph-and-regime led high-beta large-cap basket. This basket tests whether TRENT’s next move is primarily driven by graph connectivity and large-cap risk appetite rather than pure consumer demand read-throughs.

Defensive staples core with strongest peer linkage: NESTLEIND and BRITANNIA are the cleanest consumer-defensive read-throughs for HINDUNILVR, supported by top historical/rolling correlations and similar low-volatility behavior. Consumer wallet plus macro flow hypothesis: TATACONSUM offers a strong rolling-correlation staples/consumption signal, RELIANCE adds broad household-spend and index-liquidity transmission, and ICICIBANK captures consumer credit and risk-appetite spillovers. Low-volatility quality rotation test: SUNPHARMA, TCS, and NESTLEIND all overlap with HINDUNILVR through defensive/quality characteristics, low-volatility behavior, and large-cap institutional ownership patterns. This also aligns with the best prior successful setup for TECHM.

Even though prior all-IT sets were not the top performer, this remains an important controlled test because TECHM is in a sideways regime with positive 20d momentum but weak 60d momentum, a profile consistent with potential peer-led catch-up behavior. Regime-mix / market-mood transmission hypothesis: choose INFY, HEROMOTOCO, and HDFCLIFE. HEROMOTOCO is already a graph neighbor and shares the sideways regime, making it a candidate proxy for broad domestic risk appetite in quality cyclicals. This set tests whether ADANIENT’s recent momentum and resilience versus Nifty are better explained by India power-demand/capex trends than by pure Adani-group or coal-specific effects.

Consumer-defensive peer transmission set. Liquidity-and-macro spillover set. Use KOTAKBANK, RELIANCE, and AXISBANK to model ITC as a mega-cap institutional positioning vehicle. KOTAKBANK is the strongest rolling 60d correlation signal (0.603) and also a graph neighbor; AXISBANK has already appeared in prior useful experiments and adds banking-system risk appetite / FII flow information; RELIANCE contributes broad macro and market-beta leadership despite ITC’s own very low beta. Policy-sensitive defensive yield set. ONGC and POWERGRID are direct graph neighbors, and COALINDIA has featured in the better past motifs for ITC. This basket is intentionally cross-sector: all three names reflect policy/regulatory sensitivity, government-linked cash-flow perception, and defensive income positioning. Given current bearish headlines around excise/tax pressure and cigarette business concerns, this set can capture whether ITC’s return path is being driven by regulation and yield-style rotation rather than by staples peer dynamics.

Banking contagion under bearish earnings sentiment: use ICICIBANK and AXISBANK, the two strongest graph neighbors, with HDFCBANK as a high-quality same-industry anchor. This is the cleanest sector-similarity hypothesis for SBIN given negative news flow around profit miss and margin pressure. In a sideways regime with weak market mood (0.34), this trio should capture whether SBIN is trading as part of a broad private/public bank repricing rather than on purely idiosyncratic headlines. It also builds on prior success of pure-bank peer sets for SBIN.

Broader financial-services stress transmission: pair BAJFINANCE and SBILIFE, both existing graph neighbors, with SHRIRAMFIN, which has the strongest rolling 60d/120d correlation to SBIN. This tests a different hypothesis from pure banks: that bearish sentiment is propagating through credit demand, retail lending, and financial risk appetite more broadly. Given SBIN's low volatility, sideways trend, and still-positive 20d momentum, this set may detect whether the stock's moves are being governed by diversified financials positioning rather than only bank earnings read-through.

Cross-sector macro flow basket: combine ADANIPORTS, RELIANCE, and SUNPHARMA to capture cyclical, index-level, and defensive signals. ADANIPORTS is among top correlated names, RELIANCE is a same-market-cap large-cap market barometer, and SUNPHARMA is also a graph neighbor plus low-volatility defensive peer. With bearish headlines but not a full risk-off collapse, this set tests whether SBIN's forecast is better explained by rotation between economic cyclicals and defensives in a sideways market, rather than by financial-sector peers alone.

Hypothesis 1 — transport/logistics stress basket under bearish travel sentiment. Use ADANIPORTS, LT, and TMCV. If INDIGO underperforms while ADANIPORTS/LT remain stable, that points to airline-specific margin pressure; if all three weaken together, the model can capture broader industrial/travel softness consistent with the bearish mood index of 0.24.

Hypothesis 2 — demand-and-credit diagnostic basket. Use TRENT, BAJAJFINSV, and SHRIRAMFIN. Current headlines suggest possible demand moderation in travel, but INDIGO still shows positive 20d momentum despite a bearish 60d trend, so consumer and financing proxies may help identify whether the drawdown is overdone. Together they test whether weak airline sentiment is really a broader consumption-and-credit slowdown. If these proxies stay resilient while INDIGO weakens, the selloff is likely airline-specific; if they roll over too, bearish sentiment may reflect wider demand destruction.

Hypothesis 3 — graph-plus cross-sector macro basket. Use JIOFIN, ULTRACEMCO, and ETERNAL. This is a more diversified signal set designed for a large-cap stock with high current drawdown and unstable sentiment. JIOFIN is both a graph neighbor and in the same market-cap/high-volatility cohort, giving a financial-liquidity and risk-appetite signal. ULTRACEMCO is a top correlated name and shares the same bearish trend regime, serving as a domestic cyclical/investment activity barometer. ETERNAL is a graph neighbor that adds consumer-platform and urban demand sensitivity, useful when airline headlines mix cost pressure with travel-demand uncertainty. This basket tests whether INDIGO is reacting to broad risk-off conditions, domestic demand softness, or isolated airline issues; the diversity is valuable given low beta but high idiosyncratic news pressure.

Correlation-led Adani complex plus financing signal: ADANIPORTS is in a bullish trend regime with very strong recent momentum, strong relative strength vs Nifty, and mostly positive news flow. This set uses ADANIENT as the highest-confidence anchor because it is both the strongest graph neighbor and the top historical/rolling correlation name, helping capture group-level flow, promoter-news spillover, and shared sentiment transmission inside the Adani ecosystem. JIOFIN adds a high 60d rolling correlation and functions as a market-liquidity / risk-appetite proxy, useful when bullish narratives are being amplified by capital market participation. This is a sentiment-sensitive, correlation-heavy hypothesis designed to test whether ADANIPORTS is being driven by group momentum plus financial conditions rather than only port-specific fundamentals.

Industrial-capex confirmation basket with proven priors: News sentiment is mostly positive on strong Q4 results, capacity expansion, and broker optimism, so a broader infrastructure/capex read-through may explain continuation. BEL is a graph neighbor and same-sector industrial, helping capture domestic manufacturing and capex breadth that often travels with infrastructure leadership. NTPC adds a utility/power-demand signal from the same bullish trend cohort, useful for confirming whether the market is pricing a durable investment cycle rather than a one-off earnings reaction. This set also respects the graph structure and prior experiment history while staying diversified across infra execution, industrial production, and power demand.

Trade-flow and mobility demand basket: ADANIPORTS sits in a bullish regime with low beta and medium volatility, so a differentiated hypothesis is that continued upside depends on real-economy movement of goods and passengers rather than only corporate headlines. INDIGO has very strong rolling correlation and can serve as a mobility/travel demand proxy tied to broader transport activity and infrastructure utilization. MARUTI is a graph neighbor and same mega-cap / medium-volatility cohort member, capturing domestic demand, supply-chain activity, and manufacturing throughput. ONGC adds an energy and trade-flow dimension, acting as a proxy for commodity movement and macro industrial demand that can influence port cargo expectations. This set tests whether bullish market mood is validated by broad transport, consumer logistics, and energy-flow strength across the economy.

Correlation-led stability under bearish headlines: use TMPV, TMCV, and ULTRACEMCO. TMPV and TMCV are TITAN’s two strongest explicit graph/correlation anchors, while ULTRACEMCO is one of the highest rolling-correlation names across both 60d and 120d windows and also matches the mega-cap/medium-volatility neighborhood. Premium consumption read-through: use MARUTI, TRENT, and BAJAJ-AUTO. MARUTI and BAJAJ-AUTO are close sector/regime peers from the consumer cyclical bucket, and MARUTI is also a strong graph neighbor. TRENT adds a cleaner discretionary consumption signal outside autos, helping distinguish whether bearish TITAN sentiment reflects company-specific execution issues or broader premium demand softness. Given mixed semantic sentiment with downgrades and weak post-results reaction, this basket probes whether affluent urban consumption remains resilient enough to support TITAN’s bullish trend despite negative news flow.

Cross-sector liquidity and wealth-effect hypothesis: use BAJAJFINSV, KOTAKBANK, and M&M. BAJAJFINSV and KOTAKBANK capture consumer financing, wealth, and credit conditions that can influence discretionary/luxury spending, while M&M adds a domestic cyclical demand proxy and is also a graph neighbor. This is useful because TITAN has low beta and medium realized volatility, so under a bearish mood the key question is less broad market stress and more whether household balance-sheet confidence is weakening.
