Graph-plus-correlation capex transmission: Use TMPV, ULTRACEMCO, and SBIN. TMPV is the strongest graph/correlation-style link and should capture latent co-movement with LT. ULTRACEMCO has very strong 60d/120d rolling correlation and is economically tied to construction and project execution, making it a direct read-through on infrastructure demand. SBIN is both a graph neighbor and a financing proxy for large project awards turning into execution. This set fits the bullish trend regime and positive LT-specific news flow: order wins and revenue growth should transmit through materials demand and credit conditions, while mixed broader headlines are handled by adding a financial conditions node rather than only sector peers.

Sector-and-logistics confirmation with high-beta activity proxy: Use ADANIPORTS, BEL, and INDIGO. ADANIPORTS is a graph neighbor and same-sector infrastructure/logistics signal, useful for confirming whether LT strength is part of a broader capex and trade-flow upswing. BEL adds same-sector industrial/defense capex exposure, helping test whether public/institutional order momentum is spilling across Industrials. INDIGO has the highest 60d rolling correlation with LT, and acts as a real-economy mobility/activity proxy; if domestic activity remains strong, LT’s order book optimism is more likely to persist despite the recent Q4 profit dip. This is a more cyclical, demand-led hypothesis aligned with the constructive market mood.

Large-cap regime anchor with cross-sector macro confirmation: Use HDFCBANK, INFY, and TATASTEEL. HDFCBANK and INFY are graph neighbors and prior useful anchors for broad institutional risk appetite, liquidity, and market leadership; they help distinguish stock-specific strength from general large-cap trend support. TATASTEEL adds commodity and industrial-cycle sensitivity, which matters for EPC margins, project timing, and capex confidence. Given LT’s bullish sentiment skew but mixed headline backdrop, this set tests whether the stock’s momentum is being sustained by a favorable macro-equity regime plus an improving industrial input cycle, rather than only by isolated company news.

Auto-core leadership continuation: Use EICHERMOT, M&M, and HEROMOTOCO. MARUTI has bullish news sentiment, a strong market mood index (0.74), positive 20d momentum, and clear relative strength vs NIFTY, so the cleanest hypothesis is that near-term forecasting works best through tightly linked auto leaders. This set is strongly supported by graph structure and correlation data: M&M is the highest-weight graph neighbor, EICHERMOT has the strongest rolling 60d/120d correlations, and HEROMOTOCO adds same-industry breadth with meaningful graph proximity. Because MARUTI remains in a broader bearish trend regime despite the recent rally, this basket tests whether bullish sentiment is truly sector-confirmed across autos rather than being an isolated post-earnings spike.

Broad vehicle-cycle confirmation: Use EICHERMOT, M&M, and TMCV. This is a slightly wider auto ecosystem hypothesis than the pure passenger/discretionary basket. News flow is positive but not uniformly clean, with mentions of profit miss and target cuts, so adding TMCV helps test whether MARUTI’s move is being driven by a broader vehicle demand cycle rather than only premium auto peer sympathy. EICHERMOT and M&M remain the anchors because they combine top rolling correlations with strong graph relevance, while TMCV contributes same-industry exposure and can capture commercial/fleet demand, operating leverage, and broader transportation demand signals. This set is also validated by past success for MARUTI, where EICHERMOT-M&M-TMCV was one of the better-performing combinations.

Consumer-macro cross-signal basket: Use TITAN, KOTAKBANK, and M&M. MARUTI sits in Consumer Cyclical with bullish sentiment, but the longer trend regime is still bearish and current drawdown remains deep, so a diversified explanatory set may outperform a pure peer basket if the stock is trading on financing conditions and upper-middle-class consumption resilience. M&M stays as the key graph/correlation anchor from autos, TITAN adds a strong aspirational-consumption signal and is also a graph neighbor, while KOTAKBANK captures retail credit availability and financing conditions that directly affect vehicle purchases. This tests whether MARUTI’s recent strength is better explained by consumer confidence plus credit impulse rather than only auto-sector co-movement.

Hypothesis 1 — core transmission basket centered on the closest market/graph links. Use BAJFINANCE, HDFCBANK, and HDFCLIFE. BAJFINANCE is the strongest economic proxy and one of the highest correlation names for BAJAJFINSV, making it the cleanest read on Bajaj-group and credit-market spillover. HDFCBANK adds a highly correlated large-cap private bank signal from both the 60d rolling correlation list and the same medium-volatility / bearish-regime cohort, helping capture whether mixed news is being interpreted through broader financial risk appetite. HDFCLIFE is also a graph neighbor and same-sector insurer, useful because current headlines are mixed: provisional premium growth and short-term strength support the stock, while EPS miss and forecast cuts argue for caution. This set tests whether BAJAJFINSV will trade as a combination of group-financial beta plus insurance sentiment stabilization.

Hypothesis 2 — diversified financial stress and recovery basket. Use KOTAKBANK, SBIN, and SBILIFE. KOTAKBANK contributes slower-moving valuation and defensive private-bank behavior, with meaningful 120d correlation relevance and membership in the same bearish trend regime. SBIN adds a public-sector banking and policy/credit-cycle lens, which is useful when market mood is only mildly constructive (0.52) and sentiment is neutral-to-mixed rather than decisively bullish. SBILIFE is a graph neighbor and sector peer that helps isolate whether insurance/premium-growth momentum is strong enough to offset concerns around earnings quality and optimism running ahead of fundamentals. This basket is intentionally broader and less tightly coupled than the Bajaj-centric set, to test whether BAJAJFINSV weakness is actually part of a wider financial repricing.

Hypothesis 3 — momentum/market-cap cross-signal basket with one direct financial anchor. Use TMCV, GRASIM, and AXISBANK. TMCV is both a top correlated name and a graph neighbor, suggesting it may capture shared institutional flow, large-cap cyclical risk appetite, and short-term momentum spillovers. GRASIM is also in the top correlation set and same market-cap bucket, adding a diversified large-cap macro proxy that can reflect domestic growth expectations outside pure financials. AXISBANK provides the necessary financial anchor through strong 60d rolling correlation and similar volatility characteristics. Given BAJAJFINSV has positive 20d momentum but negative 60d momentum in a bearish regime, this set tests whether near-term stock strength is being driven more by broad large-cap risk rotation and momentum recovery than by purely sector-specific fundamentals. It is a deliberately cross-cluster hypothesis for mixed-sentiment conditions.

Graph-anchored continuation basket: TMCV, JIOFIN, BAJFINANCE. This is the highest-conviction finance/NBFC transmission set. TMCV is the strongest graph and historical correlation anchor and fits the vehicle-lending driver explicitly highlighted in the bullish news flow. JIOFIN is also a strong graph neighbor and already appeared in past successful runs, making it useful as a retail-credit and fintech sentiment proxy in a risk-on market mood (0.73). BAJFINANCE adds same-industry NBFC read-through, similar high-volatility behavior, and broader unsecured/consumer credit sensitivity. Hypothesis: if positive earnings, dividend signals, and debt-raising plans are interpreted as balance-sheet confidence, this trio should capture both the core vehicle-finance pulse and the broader credit-expansion bid around SHRIRAMFIN.

Correlation-led financials basket: AXISBANK, BAJAJFINSV, TMCV. This set blends the strongest near-term rolling correlations with the key graph anchor. AXISBANK and BAJAJFINSV are among the top 60d rolling correlation peers, while TMCV remains essential for the auto/vehicle finance linkage. Compared with the pure NBFC basket, this introduces a bank funding/liquidity signal through AXISBANK and diversified financial-services beta through BAJAJFINSV. In a sideways trend regime with positive 20d momentum but weaker 60d momentum, this basket tests whether SHRIRAMFIN is better forecast by broader financial-system risk appetite rather than only specialized NBFC peers. Bullish sentiment supports using pro-cyclical financials here.

Cross-sector demand-and-credit basket: TMCV, LT, SBIN. This is a more macro-sensitive hypothesis. TMCV still captures the direct vehicle-finance co-movement. LT adds capex and infrastructure demand signaling, relevant because commercial activity and equipment/vehicle demand can feed into lending growth and asset quality. SBIN contributes a large banking-system and credit-cycle proxy from the same sector, with meaningful historical correlation to the target. This diversified basket is useful because SHRIRAMFIN is in a sideways regime and may respond not only to peer NBFC moves but also to broader economic momentum. Given the constructive sentiment backdrop, this set tests whether improving market mood and business activity are the real drivers of the next move.

Sector-stress continuation hypothesis: use TCS, TECHM, and WIPRO. INFY is in a bearish trend regime with weak 20d/60d momentum and mixed-to-bearish news flow, so the cleanest signal may still come from same-industry spillovers. TCS and TECHM are the strongest graph/correlation anchors, with WIPRO adding a second-tier sector confirmation leg and breadth across IT services. This basket tests whether bearish sentiment in Indian IT remains the dominant driver and whether INFY continues to trade as part of a sector de-rating cluster rather than on idiosyncratic news.

Sector-plus-defensive rotation hypothesis: use HCLTECH, WIPRO, and HINDUNILVR. Past success suggests a mixed basket can help when sentiment is cautious and market mood is weak (0.39). HCLTECH and WIPRO transmit same-industry pressure, while HINDUNILVR acts as a defensive consumption proxy for risk-off capital rotation. If INFY weakness is accompanied by resilience in staples, this trio can separate broad risk aversion and defensive rotation from pure IT beta. It is deliberately less concentrated than a pure-IT basket while still grounded in graph-linked sector neighbors.

IT-versus-domestic macro filter hypothesis: use TCS, HDFCBANK, and LT. TCS remains the primary sector bellwether and strongest graph neighbor, while HDFCBANK is already a graph neighbor and shares the bearish trend regime, capturing broader domestic risk appetite. LT adds a capex/enterprise-demand proxy that can reflect corporate spending conditions relevant for IT services demand. Given bearish sentiment, deep drawdown, and low beta, this set tests whether INFY underperformance is better explained by sector-specific IT weakness or by a wider slowdown in domestic large-cap growth expectations.

Pure metals-and-materials transmission hypothesis. News/mood is moderately bullish (0.66) and JSWSTEEL is in a bullish trend with positive 20d momentum, so the cleanest setup is to lean into the strongest structural/graph relationships. TATASTEEL is the closest same-industry read-through and strongest graph/correlation neighbor; HINDALCO adds broader metals-cycle sensitivity and also carries a high graph weight; GRASIM brings construction/materials demand and is supported by very strong rolling correlations. This basket tests whether JSWSTEEL’s next move is mainly driven by peer metal pricing, sector earnings optimism, and domestic capex/materials strength rather than broad macro sentiment alone.

Infrastructure-cycle spillover hypothesis. Recent sentiment is constructive despite mixed headlines, with analyst optimism and long-term expansion news suggesting demand expectations may be coming from the broader industrial buildout. ULTRACEMCO is a strong graph and rolling-correlation neighbor that captures cement/infrastructure demand; ADANIPORTS adds logistics/trade throughput as a proxy for steel shipment and industrial activity; COALINDIA adds mining/input-cycle and heavy-industry demand information. This set is intentionally cross-sector but still economically linked, aiming to capture whether JSWSTEEL is trading as an infrastructure and capex beneficiary under a bullish market mood.

Low-vol bullish-regime macro leadership hypothesis. JSWSTEEL has low beta, low recent volatility, positive relative strength vs Nifty, and sits in a bullish regime, so it may be co-moving with stable large-cap leaders during risk-on phases rather than only with steel peers. BAJAJ-AUTO is already a graph neighbor and shares the bullish/low-vol profile; POWERGRID reflects domestic capex and defensive participation in a constructive tape; ONGC adds commodity-cycle and industrial-economy sensitivity without being too close to steel, preserving diversification. This basket tests whether market mood and broad cyclical leadership are the dominant short-horizon drivers.

Sector-core plus graph-risk hypothesis: use ONGC, RELIANCE, and ADANIENT. BPCL’s news flow is mixed with a mild negative tilt, driven by crude pressure, delayed results, and recent weakness, while market mood at 0.43 is neutral-risky rather than outright bearish panic. In that setup, the strongest transmission channel is still the energy complex. ONGC captures upstream crude sensitivity, RELIANCE is the closest same-industry refining/marketing anchor, and ADANIENT adds a graph-neighbor and high-beta policy/commodity risk signal. This also builds on prior successful BPCL setups that worked best with ONGC and RELIANCE at the core, while swapping in a graph-linked cyclical name for incremental information.

Correlation-macro demand hypothesis: use SBIN, NTPC, and LT. BPCL is in a bearish trend regime with negative 60-day momentum but a positive 20-day rebound, suggesting short-term moves may be influenced by broader macro stabilization rather than only oil-specific factors. SBIN and NTPC are among the stronger observed correlations, while LT is both highly correlated over longer windows and a prior useful macro proxy. Together they represent system liquidity/credit, domestic energy demand, and capex-industrial activity, all relevant for fuel consumption expectations. With mixed sentiment and only middling market mood, this basket tests whether BPCL is currently trading more as a cyclical demand proxy than as a pure refining stock.

Energy-consumption and regime-similarity hypothesis: use COALINDIA, INDIGO, and TMCV. This is a more differentiated basket aimed at capturing second-order drivers. COALINDIA keeps the domestic energy-complex linkage and was part of the best historical BPCL set. INDIGO has very high 60-day rolling correlation and is a direct aviation fuel demand proxy, which can matter for OMC earnings expectations. TMCV shares the high-volatility bucket and has elevated correlation, adding a transport/commercial vehicle lens tied to diesel demand and freight activity. Given BPCL’s mixed headlines, bearish longer trend, and recent rebound, this basket tests whether downstream demand signals and volatility-regime alignment explain near-term returns better than pure sector peers.

Hypothesis 1 - Policy-led PSU energy transmission: Use COALINDIA, NTPC, and BPCL to capture the cleanest read-through from the strongly bullish ONGC news flow. The royalty-rate cut is a government-policy shock that should lift ONGC profitability, so the best neighbors are other PSU and energy-linked names that share policy sensitivity, dividend/income investor bases, and defensive low-beta characteristics. COALINDIA and NTPC are also the two strongest graph neighbors, which strengthens the case that ONGC often co-moves with the broader PSU yield/defensive complex. BPCL adds direct oil-and-gas sector linkage and helps distinguish whether the move is sector-policy specific rather than just general market strength.

Hypothesis 2 - Defensive mega-cap rotation under bullish market mood: Use POWERGRID, ITC, and KOTAKBANK to test whether ONGC is being repriced as a low-volatility mega-cap beneficiary of improving risk appetite rather than purely as an oil story. ONGC has very low beta, very low 30d volatility, positive 20d/60d momentum, and a bullish trend regime, which makes it unusually compatible with stable institutional allocation baskets. The market mood index of 0.84 suggests broad support for quality large caps; POWERGRID and ITC are strong defensive allocation proxies, while KOTAKBANK is a graph neighbor and a high-quality mega-cap financial that can reflect broader domestic institutional flows. This set is intentionally cross-sector and should help isolate style/flow effects from commodity effects.

Hypothesis 3 - Cyclical commodity complex confirmation: Use HINDALCO, TATASTEEL, and ADANIENT to test whether ONGC's bullish breakout is also being reinforced by a wider cyclical/resource reflation trade. HINDALCO and TATASTEEL are the strongest rolling correlation names over 60d/120d, suggesting recent co-movement with ONGC despite different industries. ADANIENT contributes energy/infrastructure risk-on exposure and is also a graph neighbor, making it useful as a bridge between commodity beta and domestic macro optimism. Given the strongly positive sentiment and ONGC's relative strength versus Nifty, this basket checks whether the stock is participating in a broader pro-cyclical materials/energy leadership regime rather than only reacting to the royalty-cut catalyst.

Pure sector-contagion hypothesis: use TCS, INFY, and TECHM. This is the highest-conviction peer basket because WIPRO sits in a bearish IT-news regime, and these are its strongest graph/correlation neighbors. TCS is the top graph neighbor and strongest rolling-correlation name, INFY is consistently highly correlated and already appears in successful past runs, and TECHM adds another same-industry peer that may capture broader sector selling pressure and weak Q1 outlook transmission. With market mood weak (0.28), this set tests whether WIPRO is primarily being driven by synchronous IT-services sentiment and post-earnings disappointment across the sector.

Defensive large-cap rotation hypothesis: use INFY, SBILIFE, and GRASIM. This deliberately blends one essential sector anchor with two non-IT large-cap, lower-volatility, sideways-regime comparators. Under bearish sentiment, low beta, low 30d volatility, and WIPRO's deep drawdown, the stock may trade partly as a risk-off allocation vehicle rather than only as an IT name. INFY preserves sector information, while SBILIFE and GRASIM capture institutional rotation, liquidity preference, and defensive basket flows. This idea is supported by prior success of similar combinations and by WIPRO's sideways trend regime despite weak longer-term momentum.

Cross-signal enterprise-demand hypothesis: use HCLTECH, LT, and TCS. HCLTECH and TCS provide strong graph/industry linkage to core IT-services demand, while LT adds an external signal for enterprise capex, transformation spending, and broader corporate investment appetite. In a bearish news environment dominated by weak outlook and disappointment, WIPRO may respond not just to peer moves but also to deterioration in client spending conditions. This set is more macro-demand oriented than a pure peer basket and should help test whether WIPRO's next move is tied to spillover from enterprise spending cycles rather than only sector-relative sentiment.

Sector-plus-correlation core. Use MAXHEALTH as the primary same-industry and strongest graph neighbor, CIPLA as the strongest 60d rolling-correlation healthcare peer, and DIVISLAB as a defensive healthcare leader that also appears in the graph and 120d correlation set. With APOLLOHOSP in a bullish trend, very low beta/volatility, strong relative strength, and clearly bullish news sentiment, this basket tests whether the stock is trading mainly on healthcare-specific earnings/capacity optimism rather than broad market beta. It is the cleanest fundamental peer hypothesis and is well aligned with both graph structure and sentiment.

Low-volatility quality-compounder hypothesis. Keep MAXHEALTH for industry anchoring, then pair it with BRITANNIA and TATACONSUM, both graph neighbors and members of the same very-low-volatility bucket, with overlapping market-cap style characteristics. Given APOLLOHOSP's low beta, stable trend profile, positive momentum, and bullish market mood, this set tests whether the name is being accumulated alongside defensive growth/quality compounders rather than only healthcare peers. The idea is that positive earnings/dividend/spin-off sentiment may attract the same institutional capital that rotates into steady, low-volatility leaders.

Cross-sector institutional flow signal. Use MAXHEALTH as the healthcare anchor, BAJFINANCE as a top correlated cross-sector growth/quality proxy, and BAJAJFINSV as another correlated financial compounder to capture broader risk-on institutional allocation. This is a more macro/style-driven hypothesis: APOLLOHOSP's bullish news tone and strong relative strength may reflect not only hospital fundamentals but also participation in premium large-cap allocation baskets during constructive market mood. MAXHEALTH keeps sector information in the set, while the two financials test whether leadership is being transmitted through cross-sector growth flows rather than pure medical-care linkage.

Pure materials transmission hypothesis: use the strongest structural and graph-linked read-throughs for GRASIM in a low-volatility, sideways regime. ULTRACEMCO is the most important same-industry anchor and also shows the strongest rolling correlation profile, making it the clearest operating-demand proxy. HINDALCO and JSWSTEEL are the top graph neighbors and same-sector large-cap materials names that can capture broader commodity/capex risk appetite. This set fits the neutral-to-mixed sentiment backdrop: rather than lean on noisy single-stock news, it tests whether GRASIM trades mainly with the core materials complex despite the negative paints-management overhang.

Paints-and-construction spillover hypothesis: combine downstream competitive/news sensitivity with upstream construction demand. ASIANPAINT is relevant because current headlines include a major negative catalyst around the paints business leadership exit and valuation reassessment, so it can transmit sentiment directly into GRASIM. ULTRACEMCO captures housing/infrastructure and same-industry building-material demand, while TATASTEEL adds a graph-supported cyclical construction-input signal. In a market mood of 0.48 and mixed headlines, this basket tests whether GRASIM is being priced more as a building-materials ecosystem name than as a broad materials beta trade.

Cross-sector regime and capital-rotation hypothesis: GRASIM has low beta, low realized volatility, positive 20d momentum but weak 60d momentum, suggesting short-term rotation inside a sideways regime. Pair ULTRACEMCO as the sector anchor with SBILIFE and WIPRO, both low-volatility large caps from similar regime cohorts, to capture broader domestic risk appetite, defensive allocation, and large-cap flow dynamics. This set is intentionally more diversified than the graph-only baskets and is suited to the mixed sentiment setup, where macro positioning and style rotation may matter more than pure sector linkage.

Private-bank core with controlled diversification. Use AXISBANK, HDFCBANK, and SUNPHARMA. ICICIBANK sits in a bearish trend regime but still shows positive 20d momentum, strong relative strength vs Nifty, low beta, and low volatility, while news flow is mixed-to-slightly-positive. AXISBANK and HDFCBANK are the cleanest peer anchors: both are same-industry names, both have strong rolling correlations with ICICIBANK, and both are validated by graph structure and prior successful experiments. AXISBANK helps capture private-bank momentum transmission; HDFCBANK adds a second high-quality private-bank benchmark to distinguish stock-specific noise such as insider selling and earnings disappointment from broader sector repricing. SUNPHARMA is a low-volatility UltraMega defensive control from outside financials, useful under a neutral market mood index of 0.54 to test whether ICICIBANK is trading with a broader quality-defensive basket rather than purely on banking fundamentals. This set is a high-confidence baseline built from correlation, sector similarity, and defensive regime control.

Cross-financials risk-appetite hypothesis. Use SBIN, BAJAJFINSV, and SBILIFE. ICICIBANK’s graph neighborhood is strongest with SBIN and also includes SBILIFE and BAJFINANCE-type financial-complex links, suggesting the stock may respond to broader financial-services flows, not only private-bank peer moves. SBIN has the highest graph weight and gives a large public-sector banking read on system credit, deposit competition, and rate-sensitivity transmission. BAJAJFINSV has the strongest 60d rolling correlation among nearby financial peers and captures retail-credit and diversified financial risk appetite. SBILIFE adds an insurance/savings-flow signal that can be informative when headlines are mixed and market mood is balanced rather than strongly directional. This basket tests whether ICICIBANK’s next move is driven by financial-system sentiment rotation across banking, lending, and savings businesses, especially relevant in a low-volatility bearish regime where capital often shifts within financials rather than leaving the complex entirely.

Idiosyncratic-vs-market stress isolation using one direct bank peer and two broad macro proxies. Use KOTAKBANK, RELIANCE, and TCS. KOTAKBANK is a same-industry private-bank comparator but is less overused than AXISBANK/HDFCBANK, making it useful for testing whether ICICIBANK-specific headlines are being discounted similarly across high-quality banks. RELIANCE serves as a broad India cyclical/liquidity proxy from the same UltraMega, low-volatility universe and same bearish-regime cohort, helping identify whether moves are macro-risk or domestic growth-sensitive. TCS adds a defensive large-cap signal tied to global risk appetite, valuation sensitivity, and institutional flows; it also shares the low-volatility and bearish-regime characteristics. Given neutral sentiment with slight positive tilt, this set intentionally reduces banking collinearity and asks whether ICICIBANK’s path is better explained by a mix of private-bank quality, domestic macro leadership, and defensive institutional rotation. It is the most diversified of the three hypotheses and may work if stock-specific banking headlines are noisy.

Auto core transmission hypothesis: use HEROMOTOCO, M&M, and MARUTI as the closest liquid read-through set for BAJAJ-AUTO. HEROMOTOCO and MARUTI are both graph neighbors, while M&M has the strongest rolling 60d/120d correlation to BAJAJ-AUTO. This basket captures two-wheeler demand, passenger vehicle sentiment, rural consumption, financing conditions, and broad auto-cycle momentum. Given bullish sentiment, strong recent momentum, and positive market mood, this set tests whether BAJAJ-AUTO continues to trade primarily on sector-wide earnings strength and auto re-rating rather than idiosyncratic news alone.

Two-wheeler/value-chain purity hypothesis: use HEROMOTOCO, EICHERMOT, and TMCV to stay closer to mobility and vehicle-cycle internals. HEROMOTOCO is both a graph neighbor and a top correlated peer; EICHERMOT adds premium motorcycle demand and export/riding-cycle sensitivity; TMCV contributes commercial vehicle and transport-demand information that can reflect macro activity and replacement cycles. This is reinforced by past successful BAJAJ-AUTO experiments where HEROMOTOCO, EICHERMOT, and TMCV performed best. With sentiment strongly positive but some margin/inflation caution, this trio can reveal whether earnings optimism is confirmed across adjacent vehicle subsegments.

Cross-sector risk-on quality hypothesis: use BEL, TITAN, and HEROMOTOCO to blend one direct auto anchor with broader institutional-flow signals. BEL is a graph neighbor and low-volatility quality large-cap proxy; TITAN is a discretionary consumption leader tied to domestic premium demand; HEROMOTOCO keeps the basket grounded in the same industry. With market mood at 0.82, bullish trend regime, low volatility, and strong relative strength vs Nifty, BAJAJ-AUTO may be benefiting from both auto fundamentals and a wider rotation into high-quality consumption/industrial leaders. This set tests whether forecast power improves when combining sector linkage with market-regime confirmation.

Healthcare leadership + correlation carry. Use APOLLOHOSP as the primary anchor because it is the only same-industry peer, the strongest graph neighbor (0.72), and the top rolling correlation name across both 60d and 120d windows. Add CIPLA for same-sector, same market-cap bucket, and very-low-volatility defensive confirmation. Add TMPV as the top contemporaneous correlated name to capture short-horizon co-movement not fully explained by sector structure. This hypothesis tests whether bullish MAXHEALTH sentiment and strong market mood (0.74) transmit mainly through healthcare leaders and the closest co-movers even though MAXHEALTH remains in a bearish trend regime and sizable drawdown.

Defensive low-volatility regime basket. Use CIPLA, BRITANNIA, and TATACONSUM to model MAXHEALTH as a low-beta defensive compounder rather than a pure hospital trade. CIPLA contributes healthcare-sector confirmation and is also a graph neighbor; BRITANNIA and TATACONSUM are graph/candidate names sharing the very-low-volatility and market-cap style profile. With beta at 0.129, 30d volatility extremely low, and positive momentum/relative strength despite a bearish broader trend regime, this set tests whether favorable sentiment is being expressed through institutional rotation into stable defensives rather than only hospital-specific signals.

Hospital-plus cross-sector risk signal. Use APOLLOHOSP as the core same-industry and strongest graph-linked driver, SUNPHARMA as a large healthcare peer to capture broader medical-sector risk appetite, and M&M as a non-healthcare but same-trend-regime/correlation-linked macro signal. M&M appears among top correlated names, while APOLLOHOSP and SUNPHARMA reflect whether bullish MAXHEALTH news is reinforced by healthcare breadth. This diversified set tests a mixed hypothesis: positive sentiment may support MAXHEALTH, but because the stock is still in a bearish regime and deep drawdown, cross-sector market leadership signals may matter alongside sector confirmation.

Sector-plus-correlation anchor hypothesis: use NTPC, BPCL, and COALINDIA. NTPC is the mandatory core because it is the strongest graph neighbor by far and the only same-sector/same-industry peer, making it the cleanest transmission utility signal. BPCL and COALINDIA are both among the stronger correlation-linked candidates and fit the broader regulated power/fuel chain and PSU-flow framework. With POWERGRID in a bullish trend, strong 20d/60d momentum, very low volatility, and mildly bullish sentiment tied to grid expansion themes, this basket tests whether price discovery is being driven by an integrated energy-infrastructure complex rather than by utilities alone. COALINDIA also appears in graph neighbors, reinforcing network relevance, while BPCL shows up in top and rolling correlations, helping capture shorter-term macro-energy rotation.

Low-volatility defensive quality hypothesis: use NTPC, ITC, and ONGC. POWERGRID has very low beta, very low realized volatility, mega-cap status, and a near-high bullish regime, which often aligns with institutional rotation into stable cash-flow names when market mood is constructive but not euphoric. NTPC remains the sector anchor and strongest graph link. ITC is a graph neighbor and fits the defensive/low-volatility quality profile. ONGC is both a graph neighbor and in the same volatility bucket/trend regime, adding a commodity-linked but still defensive large-cap PSU signal. This set tests whether POWERGRID is trading as part of a broader low-volatility quality/PSU basket under mildly positive sentiment rather than purely on utility-specific news.

Capex and infrastructure breadth hypothesis: use NTPC, ADANIPORTS, and BEL. The news backdrop is bullish on grid modernization and AI/data-center power demand, suggesting POWERGRID may be responding to a wider domestic infrastructure buildout narrative. NTPC is again the structural sector control and strongest graph edge. ADANIPORTS adds a logistics/capex cycle proxy from the same bullish trend regime and mega-cap cohort, while BEL contributes a state-linked strategic manufacturing/infrastructure signal with decent correlation relevance and similar market positioning. This basket is intentionally cross-sector and tests whether POWERGRID strength reflects broader capex, PSU, and national infrastructure leadership in a positive market mood environment, not just utility fundamentals.

Sector-pure bullish confirmation basket: CIPLA, SUNPHARMA, and DRREDDY. This set leans into the strongest direct pharma read-through for DIVISLAB given constructive news flow, analyst optimism, and bullish market mood (0.74). CIPLA is the highest-confidence anchor because it is the top graph neighbor (0.527), a same-industry peer, and also shows strong 60d/120d correlation evidence. SUNPHARMA and DRREDDY are both same-industry names and graph-linked peers, helping capture whether positive sentiment in specialty/generic pharma is broadening across large listed manufacturers. With DIVISLAB in a sideways regime but carrying positive 20d and 60d momentum, this basket tests a sector-led breakout hypothesis rather than a broad-market one.

Correlation-plus-defensive healthcare basket: CIPLA, MAXHEALTH, and APOLLOHOSP. This is a co-movement hypothesis built around the graph structure and recent rolling correlations rather than only same-industry exposure. CIPLA again acts as the pharma transmission channel, while MAXHEALTH has the strongest 60d rolling correlation to DIVISLAB and APOLLOHOSP is the top 120d rolling-correlation healthcare name. All three are healthcare names, but they span pharma and providers, which helps detect whether DIVISLAB is trading with broader healthcare leadership under a bullish but low-beta, low-volatility regime. Because DIVISLAB has very low volatility and modest relative strength, this set is useful if institutional money is rotating into the healthcare complex generally rather than only drug manufacturers.

Pharma-plus-large-cap rotation basket: CIPLA, TMCV, and GRASIM. This is a diversified hypothesis that mixes one high-confidence pharma anchor with two non-healthcare large-cap regime proxies. CIPLA contributes the strongest graph and industry signal. TMCV and GRASIM both fit the same large-cap / sideways-regime profile and can capture broad institutional allocation into quality large caps during a constructive market tape. This is especially relevant because DIVISLAB has low beta (0.222), very low realized volatility, positive short-to-medium momentum, and only a modest current drawdown, suggesting it may respond to both sector optimism and cross-sector risk-on rotation.
